arguments.content:
# Developer Workforce & Compensation Trends — 2024 Stack Overflow Survey — Design Spec

## I. Project Information

| Item | Value |
| ---- | ----- |
| **Project Name** | stackoverflow_survey_2024 |
| **Canvas Format** | PPT 16:9 (1280×720) |
| **Page Count** | 8 slides |
| **Design Style** | C) Top Consulting (conclusion-first, SCQA, pyramid principle) |
| **Target Audience** | Engineering managers and HR leaders benchmarking developer compensation and workforce trends |
| **Use Case** | Executive briefing / hiring and retention strategy alignment |
| **Created Date** | 2026-04-20 |

---

## II. Canvas Specification

| Property | Value |
| -------- | ----- |
| **Format** | PPT 16:9 |
| **Dimensions** | 1280×720 |
| **viewBox** | `0 0 1280 720` |
| **Margins** | Left/right 60px, top 50px, bottom 40px |
| **Content Area** | 1160×630 (x=60, y=50) |

---

## III. Visual Theme

### Theme Style

- **Style**: Top Consulting (Exhibit-derived dark executive style)
- **Theme**: Dark theme — deep navy background, gold accent, white text
- **Tone**: Premium, authoritative, data-forward, analytical

### Color Scheme

| Role | HEX | Purpose |
| ---- | --- | ------- |
| **Background** | `#0F1724` | Page background (deep navy) |
| **Secondary bg** | `#1A2640` | Card/panel background |
| **Tertiary bg** | `#243352` | Subtle section dividers/alternating rows |
| **Primary** | `#C8A84B` | Gold — title bars, key callouts, exhibit bars |
| **Accent** | `#4A90D9` | Data blue — chart bars, scatter points, links |
| **Secondary accent** | `#E8C875` | Light gold — subtitles, secondary highlights |
| **Body text** | `#E8EDF5` | Main body text (high-contrast white-ish) |
| **Secondary text** | `#A8B8D0` | Captions, annotations, sub-labels |
| **Tertiary text** | `#6A7E9A` | Footers, page numbers |
| **Border/divider** | `#2E4060` | Card borders, separator lines |
| **Success** | `#4CAF50` | Positive trend indicators |
| **Warning** | `#EF5350` | Decline / risk indicators |

### Gradient Scheme

```xml
<!-- Gold title gradient -->
<linearGradient id="goldGradient" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="0%">
  <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#C8A84B"/>
  <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#E8C875"/>
</linearGradient>

<!-- Dark panel gradient -->
<linearGradient id="panelGradient" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="100%">
  <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#1A2640"/>
  <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#243352"/>
</linearGradient>
```

---

## IV. Typography System

### Font Plan

**Recommended preset**: P5 (English-primary)

| Role | English | Fallback |
| ---- | ------- | -------- |
| **Title** | Arial Black / Impact | Arial, sans-serif |
| **Body** | Calibri / Arial | Arial, sans-serif |
| **Code** | Consolas | Monaco, monospace |
| **Emphasis** | Arial Bold | Arial, sans-serif |

**Font stack**: `Arial Black, Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif` (titles); `Calibri, Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif` (body)

### Font Size Hierarchy

**Baseline**: Body = 18px (dense content — 6+ data points per page)

| Purpose | Size | Weight |
| ------- | ---- | ------ |
| Cover title | 54px | Bold |
| Chapter title | 42px | Bold |
| Content/slide title | 30px | Bold |
| Exhibit takeaway bar | 20px | Bold |
| Subtitle / label | 22px | SemiBold |
| **Body content** | **18px** | Regular |
| Annotation / caption | 14px | Regular |
| Footer / page number | 12px | Regular |

---

## V. Layout Principles

### Page Structure

- **Header area**: y=0 to y=90; contains title bar with gold left accent stripe (8px wide), slide title (white), exhibit takeaway text
- **Content area**: y=90 to y=680; main data visualizations, text, charts
- **Footer area**: y=680 to y=720; source attribution (left), page number (right), thin gold divider line

### Common Layout Modes

| Mode | Used On |
| ---- | ------- |
| **Full-bleed dark cover** | Slide 01 |
| **Single-column with exhibit bar** | Slides 02, 03, 07, 08 |
| **Left image + right annotation** | Slides 04, 05, 06 (chart reference images) |
| **Two-column split** | Slide 07 (company size + purchasing) |

### Spacing Specification

| Element | Current Project |
| ------- | --------------- |
| Card gap | 24px |
| Content block gap | 32px |
| Card padding | 20px |
| Card border radius | 6px |
| Icon-text gap | 10px |

---

## VI. Icon Usage Specification

### Source

- **Built-in icon library**: `templates/icons/` (640+ icons)
- **Usage method**: Placeholder format `{{icon:category/icon-name}}`

### Recommended Icon List

| Purpose | Icon | Page |
| ------- | ---- | ---- |
| Employment / workforce | `{{icon:users/users}}` | Slide 02 |
| Trend up | `{{icon:navigation/arrow-trend-up}}` | Slide 02, 03 |
| Trend down | `{{icon:navigation/arrow-trend-down}}` | Slide 02 |
| Building / company | `{{icon:business/building}}` | Slide 07 |
| Dollar / salary | `{{icon:business/dollar}}` | Slides 04, 05, 06 |
| Chart bar | `{{icon:data/chart-bar}}` | Slide 04 |
| Globe / international | `{{icon:misc/globe}}` | Slide 01 |
| Lightbulb / insight | `{{icon:misc/lightbulb}}` | Slide 08 |
| Trophy | `{{icon:misc/trophy}}` | Slide 08 |
| Checkmark | `{{icon:status/checkmark}}` | Slide 08 |
| Shopping cart / purchasing | `{{icon:business/shopping-cart}}` | Slide 07 |
| Home / remote | `{{icon:business/home}}` | Slide 03 |
| Clock / time | `{{icon:time/clock}}` | Slide 05 |

---

## VII. Chart Reference List

| Chart Type | Reference Template | Used In | Purpose |
| ---------- | ------------------ | ------- | ------- |
| horizontal_bar_chart | `templates/charts/horizontal_bar_chart.svg` | Slide 04 | Median salary ranking by developer type (custom SVG) |
| scatter_chart | `templates/charts/scatter_chart.svg` | Slides 05, 06 | Salary vs. experience correlations (custom SVG) |
| donut_chart | `templates/charts/donut_chart.svg` | Slide 02 | Employment status composition |
| grouped_bar_chart | `templates/charts/grouped_bar_chart.svg` | Slide 02 | Global vs. U.S. full-time employment comparison |
| bar_chart | `templates/charts/bar_chart.svg` | Slide 03 | Work environment 3-year trend |
| donut_chart | `templates/charts/donut_chart.svg` | Slide 07 | Company size distribution |

---

## VIII. Image Resource List

| Filename | Dimensions | Ratio | Purpose | Type | Status | Generation Description |
| -------- | ---------- | ----- | ------- | ---- | ------ | ---------------------- |
| figure_1.jpg | 1287×1542 | 0.83 | Salary by developer type bar chart reference (Slide 04) | Diagram | Existing | - |
| figure_2.jpg | 1306×1581 | 0.83 | Salary vs. experience scatter plot by developer type (Slide 05) | Diagram | Existing | - |
| figure_3.jpg | 1232×1356 | 0.91 | Salary vs. experience scatter plot by language (Slide 06) | Diagram | Existing | - |

**Image layout note**: All three figures are near-square (ratio ~0.83–0.91). Use left-right split layout — image on right ~45% width, annotations/callouts on left ~50% width. Embed using `<image>` tag in SVG via finalize_svg.py processing.

---

## IX. Content Outline

### Part 1: Survey Context

#### Slide 01 — Cover

- **Layout**: Full-bleed dark background, centered title block
- **Title**: Developer Workforce & Compensation Trends
- **Subtitle**: 2024 Stack Overflow Developer Survey
- **Key stat callout**: "65,437 Respondents · 180+ Countries · 2024"
- **Source line**: Source: Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2024 | survey.stackoverflow.co/2024/work

#### Slide 02 — Employment Status

- **Layout**: Single column, exhibit takeaway bar at top, content below
- **Title**: 84% of Developers Are Working, but Full-Time Employment Dips in the U.S.
- **Exhibit bar takeaway**: U.S. full-time employment fell 4 pp YoY — plan for greater contractor reliance
- **Chart**: Grouped bar chart — Global vs. U.S. full-time employment (69% vs. 64.8%)
- **KPI cards**: Full-time 69% | Freelance/Contract 16.4% | Student 13.2%
- **Callout**: Ukraine & U.K. lean toward contracting; Germany & India toward student status
- **Source**: 65,437 respondents

#### Slide 03 — Work Environment

- **Layout**: Single column, exhibit bar, bar chart
- **Title**: In-Person Work Rises to 20% While Hybrid Holds Steady at 42%
- **Exhibit bar takeaway**: Third consecutive year of in-person growth — RTO trend is real but slow
- **Chart**: Grouped bar chart — 3-year trend (2022/2023/2024) for Remote / Hybrid / In-Person
  - Remote: 2022 n/a → 2023 ~46% → 2024 38%
  - Hybrid: 42% consistent
  - In-person: 15% → 16% → 20%
- **Callout**: Hybrid still dominant at 42%; in-person up 5pp in 2 years
- **Source**: Stack Overflow Survey 2024

#### Slide 04 — Salary by Developer Type

- **Layout**: Left text/callouts (50%) + right embedded figure_1.jpg (45%)
- **Title**: Senior Executives and Dev Advocates Top $124K+ Median Salary
- **Exhibit bar takeaway**: SRE and Cloud Infra are the highest-paid purely technical roles at $97–99K
- **Reference image**: figure_1.jpg (horizontal bar chart — top 10 developer types by median salary)
- **Key data callouts** (left panel):
  - Senior Executive: $127,388 | ~17 yrs exp
  - Dev Advocate: $124,203 | ~16 yrs exp
  - Manager: $115,999 | ~15 yrs exp
  - SRE: $99,099 | ~10 yrs exp
  - Full-stack: $63,333 | ~10 yrs exp
  - Front-end: $48,787 | ~8 yrs exp
- **Note**: 22,677 salary responses (34.7% response rate)
- **Source**: Stack Overflow Survey 2024

#### Slide 05 — Experience vs. Salary

- **Layout**: Left annotations (45%) + right embedded figure_2.jpg (50%)
- **Title**: Experience Pays: Top Roles Combine 14+ Years with Six-Figure Salaries
- **Exhibit bar takeaway**: Senior roles cluster upper-right; Student is a stark outlier at $15K / 2 yrs
- **Reference image**: figure_2.jpg (scatter plot — median salary vs. avg years exp by developer type)
- **Callout annotations** (left panel):
  - Upper-right cluster: Senior Exec ($127K, 17yr), Dev Advocate ($124K, 16yr), Manager ($116K, 15yr)
  - Mid-range: SRE ($99K, 10yr), Cloud Infra ($97K, 13yr), Dev Experience ($109K, 12yr)
  - Low outlier: Student ($15K, 2yr)
  - Insight: R² positive — experience explains significant pay variance
- **Source**: Stack Overflow Survey 2024

#### Slide 06 — Salary by Language

- **Layout**: Left annotations (45%) + right embedded figure_3.jpg (50%)
- **Title**: Erlang & Clojure Developers Earn >$95K; Dart & Prolog Below $45K
- **Exhibit bar takeaway**: Niche functional languages command $30K+ premium over mainstream JS/PHP
- **Reference image**: figure_3.jpg (scatter plot — salary vs. experience by programming language)
- **Callout annotations** (left panel):
  - Top earners: Erlang ~$97K, Clojure ~$95K, Elixir ~$93K
  - Mid-range: Go ~$76K, Python ~$67K, JavaScript ~$64K
  - Low earners: PHP ~$49K, Dart ~$44K, Prolog ~$43K
  - Note: Overall salary range dropped ~$10K vs. 2023 (now $60–75K avg vs. $70–85K)
- **Source**: Stack Overflow Survey 2024

#### Slide 07 — Company Size & Purchasing Influence

- **Layout**: Two-column — left: company size donut/bar chart; right: purchasing influence KPI cards
- **Title**: 47% Work at Sub-100 Orgs; 62% Influence Tech Purchases

## IV. Typography System

### Font Plan

**Recommended preset**: P5 (English-primary)

| **Title** | Arial Black / Impact | Arial, sans-serif |
| **Body** | Calibri / Arial | Arial, sans-serif |
| **Code** | Consolas | Monaco, monospace |
| **Emphasis** | Arial Bold | Arial, sans-serif |

**Font stack**: `Arial Black, Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif` (titles); `Calibri, Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif` (body)

### Font Size Hierarchy

**Baseline**: Body = 18px (dense content — 6+ data points per page)

| Purpose | Size | Weight |
| ------- | ---- | ------ |
| Cover title | 54px | Bold |
| Chapter title | 42px | Bold |
| Content/slide title | 30px | Bold |
| Exhibit takeaway bar | 20px | Bold |
| Subtitle / label | 22px | SemiBold |
| **Body content** | **18px** | Regular |
| Annotation / caption | 14px | Regular |
| Footer / page number | 12px | Regular |

---

## V. Layout Principles

### Page Structure

- **Header area**: y=0 to y=90; contains title bar with gold left accent stripe (8px wide), slide title (white), exhibit takeaway text
- **Content area**: y=90 to y=680; main data visualizations, text, charts
- **Footer area**: y=680 to y=720; source attribution (left), page number (right), thin gold divider line

### Common Layout Modes

| Mode | Used On |
| ---- | ------- |
| **Full-bleed dark cover** | Slide 01 |
| **Single-column with exhibit bar** | Slides 02, 03, 07, 08 |
| **Left image + right annotation** | Slides 04, 05, 06 (chart reference images) |
| **Two-column split** | Slide 07 (company size + purchasing) |

### Spacing Specification

| Element | Current Project |
| ------- | --------------- |
| Card gap | 24px |
| Content block gap | 32px |
| Card padding | 20px |
| Card border radius | 6px |
| Icon-text gap | 10px |

### Source

- **Built-in icon library**: `templates/icons/` (640+ icons)
- **Usage method**: Placeholder format `{{icon:category/icon-name}}`

### Recommended Icon List

**Image layout note**: All three figures are near-square (ratio ~0.83–0.91). Use left-right split layout — image on right ~45% width, annotations/callouts on left ~50% width. Embed using `<image>` tag in SVG via finalize_svg.py processing.

---

## IX. Content Outline

### Part 1: Survey Context

#### Slide 01 — Cover

- **Layout**: Full-bleed dark background, centered title block
- **Title**: Developer Workforce & Compensation Trends
- **Subtitle**: 2024 Stack Overflow Developer Survey
- **Key stat callout**: "65,437 Respondents · 180+ Countries · 2024"
- **Source line**: Source: Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2024 | survey.stackoverflow.co/2024/work

#### Slide 02 — Employment Status

- **Layout**: Single column, exhibit takeaway bar at top, content below
- **Title**: 84% of Developers Are Working, but Full-Time Employment Dips in the U.S.
- **Exhibit bar takeaway**: U.S. full-time employment fell 4 pp YoY — plan for greater contractor reliance
- **Chart**: Grouped bar chart — Global vs. U.S. full-time employment (69% vs. 64.8%)
- **KPI cards**: Full-time 69% | Freelance/Contract 16.4% | Student 13.2%
- **Callout**: Ukraine & U.K. lean toward contracting; Germany & India toward student status
- **Source**: 65,437 respondents

#### Slide 03 — Work Environment

- **Layout**: Single column, exhibit bar, bar chart
- **Title**: In-Person Work Rises to 20% While Hybrid Holds Steady at 42%
- **Exhibit bar takeaway**: Third consecutive year of in-person growth — RTO trend is real but slow
- **Chart**: Grouped bar chart — 3-year trend (2022/2023/2024) for Remote / Hybrid / In-Person
  - Remote: 2022 n/a → 2023 ~46% → 2024 38%
  - Hybrid: 42% consistent
  - In-person: 15% → 16% → 20%
- **Callout**: Hybrid still dominant at 42%; in-person up 5pp in 2 years
- **Source**: Stack Overflow Survey 2024

#### Slide 04 — Salary by Developer Type

- **Layout**: Left text/callouts (50%) + right embedded figure_1.jpg (45%)
- **Title**: Senior Executives and Dev Advocates Top $124K+ Median Salary
- **Exhibit bar takeaway**: SRE and Cloud Infra are the highest-paid purely technical roles at $97–99K
- **Reference image**: figure_1.jpg (horizontal bar chart — top 10 developer types by median salary)
- **Key data callouts** (left panel):
  - Senior Executive: $127,388 | ~17 yrs exp
  - Dev Advocate: $124,203 | ~16 yrs exp
  - Manager: $115,999 | ~15 yrs exp
  - SRE: $99,099 | ~10 yrs exp
  - Full-stack: $63,333 | ~10 yrs exp
  - Front-end: $48,787 | ~8 yrs exp
- **Note**: 22,677 salary responses (34.7% response rate)
- **Source**: Stack Overflow Survey 2024

#### Slide 05 — Experience vs. Salary

- **Layout**: Left annotations (45%) + right embedded figure_2.jpg (50%)
- **Title**: Experience Pays: Top Roles Combine 14+ Years with Six-Figure Salaries
- **Exhibit bar takeaway**: Senior roles cluster upper-right; Student is a stark outlier at $15K / 2 yrs
- **Reference image**: figure_2.jpg (scatter plot — median salary vs. avg years exp by developer type)
- **Callout annotations** (left panel):
  - Upper-right cluster: Senior Exec ($127K, 17yr), Dev Advocate ($124K, 16yr), Manager ($116K, 15yr)
  - Mid-range: SRE ($99K, 10yr), Cloud Infra ($97K, 13yr), Dev Experience ($109K, 12yr)
  - Low outlier: Student ($15K, 2yr)
  - Insight: R² positive — experience explains significant pay variance
- **Source**: Stack Overflow Survey 2024

#### Slide 06 — Salary by Language

- **Layout**: Left annotations (45%) + right embedded figure_3.jpg (50%)
- **Title**: Erlang & Clojure Developers Earn >$95K; Dart & Prolog Below $45K
- **Exhibit bar takeaway**: Niche functional languages command $30K+ premium over mainstream JS/PHP
- **Reference image**: figure_3.jpg (scatter plot — salary vs. experience by programming language)
- **Callout annotations** (left panel):
  - Top earners: Erlang ~$97K, Clojure ~$95K, Elixir ~$93K
  - Mid-range: Go ~$76K, Python ~$67K, JavaScript ~$64K
  - Low earners: PHP ~$49K, Dart ~$44K, Prolog ~$43K
  - Note: Overall salary range dropped ~$10K vs. 2023 (now $60–75K avg vs. $70–85K)
- **Source**: Stack Overflow Survey 2024

#### Slide 07 — Company Size & Purchasing Influence

- **Layout**: Two-column — left: company size donut/bar chart; right: purchasing influence KPI cards
- **Title**: 47% Work at Sub-100 Orgs; 62% Influence Tech Purchases
- **Exhibit bar takeaway**: Individual contributors, not just management, drive vendor decisions
- **Left column — Company Size** (42,827 respondents):
  - Freelancer/solo: 6.1%
  - 2–9: 10.4% | 10–19: 8.9% | 20–99: 21.2% → Sub-100 total: 46.6%
  - 100–499: 18.5% | 500–999: 6.7% | 1,000–4,999: 11.0%
  - 5,000–9,999: 3.8% | 10,000+: 11.4%
- **Right column — Purchasing Influence**:
  - 62% have influence over tech purchases
  - Senior executives: 99% influence | Eng managers: 87% | Product managers: 77%
  - 60% prefer build-and-buy approach
  - Top evaluation methods: free trial (75%), ask other developers (73%)
- **Source**: Stack Overflow Survey 2024

#### Slide 08 — Key Takeaways

- **Layout**: Single column, exhibit bar, 5-point action list with icons
- **Title**: Takeaways: What These Trends Mean for Hiring & Retention
- **Exhibit bar takeaway**: Act on these five signals to stay ahead in talent acquisition and retention
- **Content** (5 actionable insights):
  1. **Full-time softening**: U.S. FT employment down 4pp — build flexible contractor pipelines alongside FTE hiring
  2. **Hybrid is durable**: 42% hybrid, in-person rising to 20% — RTO mandates risk attrition; offer structured hybrid
  3. **Premium roles command premium pay**: SRE ($99K), DevRel ($124K), and Managers ($116K) require calibrated comp bands — benchmark against 15+ yr experience profiles
  4. **Language choice drives pay**: Erlang/Clojure/Elixir devs earn >$93K vs. $64K for JS — factor language stack into offer benchmarks
  5. **Engage developers in vendor decisions**: 62% influence purchases; 75% prefer free trials — involve ICs in tooling evaluations, not just management
- **Source**: Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2024 | survey.stackoverflow.co/2024/work

---

## X. Speaker Notes Requirements

- **File naming**: `notes/total.md` master document with `# Slide N` headings
- **Duration**: 20 minutes total (~2.5 min per slide)
- **Style**: Professional, consulting-appropriate, conclusion-first
- **Purpose**: Inform and persuade engineering leaders on compensation benchmarking

---

## XI. Technical Constraints Reminder

### SVG Generation Must Follow:

1. viewBox: `0 0 1280 720`
2. Background uses `<rect>` elements only
3. Text wrapping uses `<tspan>` — `<foreignObject>` FORBIDDEN
4. Transparency uses `fill-opacity` / `stroke-opacity` — `rgba()` FORBIDDEN
5. FORBIDDEN: `clipPath`, `mask`, `<style>`, `class`, `foreignObject`
6. FORBIDDEN: `textPath`, `animate*`, `script`, `marker`/`marker-end`
7. Arrows use `<polygon>` triangles instead of `<marker>`
8. Image files referenced as `../images/figure_X.jpg` relative paths in SVG

### PPT Compatibility Rules:

- `<g opacity="...">` FORBIDDEN — set opacity on each child element individually
- Inline styles only; external CSS and `@font-face` FORBIDDEN

---

## XII. Design Checklist

### Pre-generation

- [x] 8 slides mapped to task_input.json slide IDs
- [x] All data sourced from source_brief.md only
- [x] Charts aligned with available chart types
- [x] Images analyzed and layout mode selected
- [x] Icon names verified against icons_index.json

### Post-generation

- [ ] viewBox = `0 0 1280 720`
- [ ] No `<foreignObject>` elements
- [ ] All text >= 14px
- [ ] Content within safe area
- [ ] Footer on every slide with source attribution
- [ ] Gold accent consistent across all slides

---

## XIII. Next Steps

1. ✅ Design spec complete
2. **Image approach**: B) User-provided (figure_1.jpg, figure_2.jpg, figure_3.jpg already in `images/`)
3. **Next step**: Invoke **Executor** (Top Consulting style) to generate SVGs

# Executor Common Guidelines

> Style-specific content is in the corresponding `executor-{style}.md`. Technical constraints are in shared-standards.md.

---

## 1. Template Adherence Rules

If template files exist in the project's `templates/` directory, the template structure must be followed:

| Page Type | Corresponding Template | Adherence Rules |
|-----------|----------------------|-----------------|
| Cover | `01_cover.svg` | Inherit background, decorative elements, layout structure; replace placeholder content |
| Chapter | `02_chapter.svg` | Inherit numbering style, title position, decorative elements |
| Content | `03_content.svg` | Inherit header/footer styles; **content area may be freely laid out** |
| Ending | `04_ending.svg` | Inherit background, thank-you message position, contact info layout |
| TOC | `02_toc.svg` | **Optional**: Inherit TOC title, list styles |

### Page-Template Mapping Declaration (Required Output)

Before generating each page, you must explicitly output which template (or "free design") is used:

```
📝 **Template mapping**: `templates/01_cover.svg` (or "None (free design)")
🎯 **Adherence rules / layout strategy**: [specific description]
```

- **Content pages**: Templates only define header and footer; the content area is freely laid out by the Executor
- **No template**: Generate entirely per the Design Specification & Content Outline

---

## 2. Design Parameter Confirmation (Mandatory Step)

> Before generating the first SVG page, you **must review the key design parameters from the Design Specification & Content Outline** to ensure all subsequent generation strictly follows the spec.

Must output confirmation including: canvas dimensions, body font size, color scheme (primary/secondary/accent HEX values), font plan.

**Why is this step mandatory?** Prevents the "spec says one thing, execution does another" disconnect.

---

## 3. Execution Guidelines

- **Proximity principle**: Place related elements close together to form visual groups; increase spacing between unrelated groups to reinforce logical structure
- **Absolute spec adherence**: Strictly follow the color, layout, canvas format, and typography parameters in the spec
- **Follow template structure**: If templates exist, inherit the template's visual framework
- **Phased batch generation** (recommended):
  1. **Visual Construction Phase**: Generate all SVG pages continuously, ensuring high consistency in design style and layout coordinates (Visual Consistency)
  2. **Logic Construction Phase**: After all SVGs are finalized, batch-generate speaker notes to ensure narrative coherence (Narrative Continuity)
- **Technical specifications**: See [shared-standards.md](shared-standards.md) for SVG technical constraints and PPT compatibility rules

### SVG File Naming Convention

File naming format: `<number>_<page_name>.svg`

- **Chinese content** → Chinese naming: `01_封面.svg`, `02_目录.svg`, `03_核心优势.svg`
- **English content** → English naming: `01_cover.svg`, `02_agenda.svg`, `03_key_benefits.svg`
- **Number rules**: Two-digit numbers, starting from 01
- **Page name**: Concise and descriptive, matching the page title in the Design Specification & Content Outline

---

## 4. Icon Usage

Four approaches: **A: Emoji** (`<text>🚀</text>`) | **B: AI-generated** (SVG basic shapes) | **C: Built-in library** (`templates/icons/` 640+ icons, recommended) | **D: Custom** (user-specified)

**Built-in icons — Placeholder method (recommended)**:

```xml
<use data-icon="chart-bar" x="100" y="200" width="48" height="48" fill="#005587"/>
```

> No need to manually run `embed_icons.py`; `finalize_svg.py` post-processing tool will auto-embed icons.

**Common icons**: `chart-bar` `arrow-trend-up` `users` `cog` `circle-checkmark` `target` `clock` `file` `dollar` `lightbulb`

> ⚠️ **Icon validation rule**: If the Design Specification includes an icon inventory list, Executor may **only** use icons from that approved list. Using icon names not in the index is FORBIDDEN — verify against `templates/icons/icons_index.json` if uncertain.

Full index: `templates/icons/README.md`

---

## 5. Chart Reference

When the Design Spec includes a **VII. Chart Reference List**, read the referenced SVG templates from `templates/charts/` to understand common chart patterns.

**Adaptation rules**:
- **Must preserve**: Chart type (bar/line/pie etc.) as specified in the Design Spec
- **Must adapt**: Data values, labels, colors (match the project's color scheme), and dimensions to fit the page layout
- **May adjust**: Axis ranges, grid lines, legend position, spacing — as long as the chart remains accurate and readable
- **Must NOT**: Change chart type without Design Spec justification, or remove data points specified in the outline

> Chart templates: `templates/charts/` (33 types). Index: `templates/charts/charts_index.json`

---

## 6. Image Handling

Handle images based on their status in the Design Specification's "Image Resource List":

| Status | Source | Handling |
|--------|--------|----------|
| **Existing** | User-provided | Reference images directly from `../images/` directory |
| **AI-generated** | Generated by Image_Generator | Images already in `../images/`, reference directly |
| **Placeholder** | Not yet prepared | Use dashed border placeholder |

**Reference**: `<image href="../images/xxx.png" ... preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>`

**Placeholder**: Dashed border `<rect stroke-dasharray="8,4" .../>` + description text

---

## 7. Font Usage

Apply corresponding fonts for different text roles based on the font plan in the Design Specification & Content Outline:

| Role | Chinese Recommended | English Recommended |
|------|--------------------|--------------------|
| Title font | Microsoft YaHei / KaiTi / SimHei | Arial / Georgia |
| Body font | Microsoft YaHei / SimSun | Calibri / Times |
| Emphasis font | SimHei | Arial Black / Consolas |
| Annotation font | Microsoft YaHei / SimSun | Arial / Times |

---

## 8. Speaker Notes Generation Framework

### Task 1. Generate Complete Speaker Notes Document

After **all SVG pages are generated and finalized**, enter the "Logic Construction Phase" and generate the complete speaker notes document in `notes/total.md`.

**Why not generate page-by-page?** Batch-writing notes allows planning transitions like a script, ensuring coherent presentation logic.

**Format**: Each page starts with `# <number>_<page_title>`, separated by `---` between pages. Each page includes: script text (2-5 sentences), `Key points: ① ② ③`, `Duration: X minutes`. Except for the first page, each page's text starts with a `[Transition]` phrase.

**Basic stage direction markers** (common to all styles):

| Marker | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `[Pause]` | Whitespace after key content, letting the audience absorb |
| `[Transition]` | Standalone paragraph at the start of each page's text, bridging from the previous page |

> Each style may extend with additional markers (`[Interactive]`/`[Data]`/`[Scan Room]`/`[Benchmark]` etc.), see `executor-{style}.md`.

**Requirements**:

- Notes should be conversational and flow naturally
- Highlight each page's core information and presentation key points
- Users can manually edit and override in the `notes/` directory

### Task 2. Split Into Per-Page Note Files

Automatically split `notes/total.md` into individual speaker note files in the `notes/` directory.

**File naming convention**:

- **Recommended**: Match SVG names (e.g., `01_cover.svg` → `notes/01_cover.md`)
- **Compatible**: Also supports `slide01.md` format (backward compatibility)

---

## 9. Next Steps After Completion

> **Auto-continuation**: After Visual Construction Phase (all SVG pages) and Logic Construction Phase (all notes) are complete, the Executor proceeds directly to the post-processing pipeline.

**Post-processing & Export** (see [shared-standards.md](shared-standards.md)):

```bash
# 1. Split speaker notes
python3 scripts/total_md_split.py <project_path>

# 2. SVG post-processing (auto-embed icons, images, etc.)
python3 scripts/finalize_svg.py <project_path>

# 3. Export PPTX
python3 scripts/svg_to_pptx.py <project_path> -s final
# Default: generates native shapes (.pptx) + SVG reference (_svg.pptx)
```

1	# Executor Consultant Top — Top-tier Consulting Style (MBB Level)
2	
3	> Common guidelines: executor-base.md. Technical constraints: shared-standards.md.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## Role Definition
8	
9	An MBB-level (McKinsey / Bain / BCG) top-tier consulting style SVG design executor. Suitable for strategic planning, board presentations, investment roadshows, C-suite decision support, and other **premium consulting** scenarios. Core characteristics: data-driven insights, pyramid-structured narrative, extreme simplicity. Output targets C-level decision-makers.
10	
11	---
12	
13	## SCQA Framework (Narrative Structure)
14	
15	Every MBB-level presentation follows the SCQA narrative structure:
16	
17	| Element | Purpose | Typical Pages |
18	|---------|---------|---------------|
19	| **S - Situation** | Establish shared context | Cover / Pages 1-2 |
20	| **C - Complication** | Introduce the problem / tension | Pages 2-3 |
21	| **Q - Question** | The implicit or explicit question to solve | Transition page |
22	| **A - Answer** | Core solution | All body pages |
23	
24	**Page sequencing**: Cover embodies S+C → Executive Summary answers Q → Chapters develop A → Closing revisits S
25	
26	**Title writing**:
27	
28	| SCQA Element | Weak Title | MBB-level Title |
29	|-------------|------------|-----------------|
30	| S | "Industry Background" | "Digital penetration surpasses 60%, industry enters deep waters" |
31	| C | "Challenges Faced" | "Yet three structural contradictions constrain scaled deployment" |
32	| Q | "Strategic Question" | "How to move from pilot to full deployment within 18 months?" |
33	| A | "Solution" | "Three-phase path: Focus, Expand, Scale" |
34	
35	---
36	
37	## Data Contextualization (Never Present Data in Isolation)
38	
39	> **Golden Rule**: Never display a single data point in isolation. Every number needs context.
40	
41	| Method | Pattern | Visual Implementation |
42	|--------|---------|----------------------|
43	| **Time comparison** | "From X to Y" | Line chart + arrow annotating magnitude of change |
44	| **Benchmark** | "X vs industry average Y" | Bar chart with gray dashed baseline |
45	| **Competitive comparison** | "Us X vs Competitor Y" | Side-by-side bar chart, highlight own data |
46	| **Target gap** | "Actual X / Target Y" | Progress bar + gap annotation |
47	| **Ranking** | "Ranked #N of M" | Horizontal bar chart + highlight marker |
48	
49	**Data annotation three essentials**: Every data visualization must include (1) The value itself (large bold font) (2) Comparison reference (baseline / prior period / competitor) (3) Meaning interpretation ("So what?")
50	
51	```xml
52	<text x="160" y="280" text-anchor="middle" font-size="42" font-weight="bold" fill="#1E293B">97.3%</text>
53	<text x="160" y="310" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="#64748B">Industry avg 82% | Competitor A 89%</text>
54	<text x="160" y="335" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" fill="#059669">Leading industry by 15.3 percentage points</text>
55	```
56	
57	---
58	
59	## Pyramid Principle (Conclusion First)
60	
61	> Executives don't care about your *process* — they care about *results*.
62	
63	```
64	         ┌─────────────────┐
65	         │  Core Conclusion │   ← Page title / Takeaway
66	         └────────┬────────┘
67	      ┌───────────┼───────────┐
68	  ┌───┴───┐  ┌───┴───┐  ┌───┴───┐
69	  │ Arg 1 │  │ Arg 2 │  │ Arg 3 │   ← Key supporting points
70	  └───────┘  └───────┘  └───────┘
71	```
72	
73	| Level | Position | Font Size |
74	|-------|----------|-----------|
75	| Core conclusion | Takeaway Box | 16-18px bold |
76	| Arguments | Content area body | 14-16px |
77	| Supporting data | Charts / cards | 12-14px |
78	
79	**Contrast**: Title "Market Research Results" (wrong) → "Metaverse needs 5-10 years to reach scale" (right); Body "We researched... and found..." (wrong) → "Three arguments: (1)... (2)... (3)..." (right)
80	
81	---
82	
83	## MBB-level Layout Patterns
84	
85	### Content Page Standard Structure (1280x720)
86	
87	```
88	┌──────────────────────────────────┐
89	│ Gradient top bar (0,0 → 1280,6)  │
90	├──────────────────────────────────┤
91	│ Assertion title (x=40, y=50, 24px)│
92	├──────────────────────────────────┤
93	│ Takeaway Box (x=40, y=75,        │  ← Dark background + white text, one-sentence conclusion
94	│   w=1200, h=45)                  │
95	├──────────────────────────────────┤
96	│ Content area (x=40, y=140,       │  ← Charts / data / analysis
97	│   w=1200, h=520)                 │
98	├──────────────────────────────────┤
99	│ Source | CONFIDENTIAL | Page #    │  ← y=700, 10px
100	└──────────────────────────────────┘
101	```
102	
103	### Strategic Roadmap
104	
105	Three phases laid out horizontally, `<rect rx="8">` + title + action list, `<polygon>` arrows connecting:
106	
107	```
108	Focus Core (0-6mo)  ──>  Expand Capability (6-12mo)  ──>  Scale Up (12-18mo)
109	x=40,w=380              x=450,w=380                     x=860,w=380
110	```
111	
112	### Benchmarking Matrix
113	
114	Horizontal table; own row highlighted in theme color, others in gray. Leading indicators marked green, lagging marked red. Use `<circle>` or `<rect>` to build score points.
115	
116	### Waterfall Chart (Change Attribution)
117	
118	Start → increase/decrease factors → End. Positive factors green bars, negative factors red bars, start/end points dark bars, cumulative line as dashed connector.
119	
120	---
121	
122	## Strategic Use of Color
123	
124	MBB-level color usage is extremely restrained — color serves information:
125	
126	| Purpose | Method |
127	|---------|--------|
128	| **Focus** | Target data in theme color, everything else gray |
129	| **Reduce cognitive load** | Same series differentiated by opacity (`fill-opacity` 1.0/0.6/0.3) |
130	| **Semantics** | Green = positive, Red = negative, Gray = baseline |
131	| **Branding** | Gradient top bar / decorative lines in brand color |
132	
133	**Commandments**: No more than 3 primary colors; accent color used at most 2-3 places globally; data series use same-hue depth variations, not different colors; background white or very light gray.
134	
135	---
136	
137	## Chart vs Table Selection Matrix
138	
139	| Scenario | Recommended Form | Reason |
140	|----------|-----------------|--------|
141	| Comparing 2-7 categories | **Bar chart** | Visual comparison is intuitive |
142	| Time trends | **Line chart** | Time series clarity |
143	| Precise values / large rankings | **Table** | 50 data points in a bar chart would be chaotic |
144	| Proportional composition | **Donut chart** | More modern than pie charts |
145	| Two-dimensional positioning | **2x2 matrix** | Strategic quadrant analysis |
146	| Change attribution | **Waterfall chart** | Factor decomposition |
147	
148	---
149	
150	## Speaker Notes Style
151	
152	### Narrative Tone
153	
154	Targeting **executives / decision-makers**. Pyramid structure — every sentence carries information. Composed, authoritative, and insightful tone.
155	
156	### Stage Direction Markers
157	
158	| Marker | Purpose | Example |
159	|--------|---------|---------|
160	| `[Pause]` | Silence after key insight, let executives absorb | "This means we are missing a billion-dollar market. [Pause]" |
161	| `[Scan Room]` | Observe decision-makers' reactions, decide whether to elaborate | "[Scan Room] If there are questions, I can elaborate." |
162	| `[Data]` | Conversational number delivery | "[Data] 63% → nearly two-thirds" |
163	| `[Benchmark]` | Emphasize comparison baseline | "[Benchmark] Compared to the industry average of 12%, our 23% is nearly double" |
164	| `[Transition]` | Bridge from previous page, at start of each page's text | "[Transition] Building on the strategic framework, let's drill into the implementation path." |
165	
166	### Notes Writing Guidelines
167	
168	- **Pyramid structure**: Conclusion → Arguments → Details
169	- **Data contextualization**: Every number has a comparison reference
170	- **Executive language**: "The strategic implication is...", "The core insight is..."
171	- **Flex mechanism**: Annotate "content that can be skipped if time is tight" for flexible duration
172	- **Key points structure**: `Key points: (1) Core insight (2) Data support (3) Strategic implication`
173	
174	### Notes Example
175	
176	```markdown
177	# 03_strategic_path
178	
179	[Transition] Having clarified the problem and the opportunity, now comes the most critical part — our response path.
180	
181	We recommend a three-phase strategy. [Pause]
182	
183	Phase one: Focus. Over the next six months, concentrate resources on conquering the Eastern China market.
184	[Data] Eastern China contributes nearly two-thirds of industry growth, [Benchmark] yet our penetration rate is only half of Competitor A's. [Pause]
185	
186	Phase two: Expand. Use Eastern China as a template, replicate to Southern and Northern China.
187	Phase three: Scale. Leverage a digital platform for nationwide coverage.
188	
189	[Scan Room] The resource allocation for phase one is in the appendix — would you like me to walk through it now?
190	
191	Key points: (1) Focus-Expand-Scale three-phase approach (2) Data-backed Eastern China priority (3) 18-month full deployment
192	Duration: 3 minutes
193	Flex: [If time is tight, skip phase two and three details and go straight to financial impact]
194	```
195	
196	---
197	
198	## MBB-level Quality Checklist Supplement
199	
200	### Content Level
201	
202	- [ ] **SCQA complete**: Overall follows Situation-Complication-Question-Answer structure
203	- [ ] **Data contextualized**: Every data point has a comparison reference
204	- [ ] **Conclusion first**: Every page's Takeaway Box has a one-sentence conclusion
205	- [ ] **MECE principle**: Categorized analysis is mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive
206	
207	### Visual Level
208	
209	- [ ] **Color with intent**: Colors serve information delivery
210	- [ ] **Ample whitespace**: Not crowded; information can "breathe"
211	- [ ] **Visual hierarchy**: Conclusion > Arguments > Details, differentiated by font size/weight
212	- [ ] **Brand consistency**: Gradient top bar and footer unified throughout
213	
214	### Notes Level
215	
216	- [ ] **Pyramid structure**: Every page is conclusion-first
217	- [ ] **Stage markers complete**: [Pause] and [Scan Room] at key positions
218	- [ ] **Flex content annotated**: Supports flexible duration
219

# Executor Consultant Top — Top-tier Consulting Style (MBB Level)

> Common guidelines: executor-base.md. Technical constraints: shared-standards.md.

---

## Role Definition

An MBB-level (McKinsey / Bain / BCG) top-tier consulting style SVG design executor. Suitable for strategic planning, board presentations, investment roadshows, C-suite decision support, and other **premium consulting** scenarios. Core characteristics: data-driven insights, pyramid-structured narrative, extreme simplicity. Output targets C-level decision-makers.

---

## SCQA Framework (Narrative Structure)

Every MBB-level presentation follows the SCQA narrative structure:

| Element | Purpose | Typical Pages |
|---------|---------|---------------|
| **S - Situation** | Establish shared context | Cover / Pages 1-2 |
| **C - Complication** | Introduce the problem / tension | Pages 2-3 |
| **Q - Question** | The implicit or explicit question to solve | Transition page |
| **A - Answer** | Core solution | All body pages |

**Page sequencing**: Cover embodies S+C → Executive Summary answers Q → Chapters develop A → Closing revisits S

**Title writing**:

| SCQA Element | Weak Title | MBB-level Title |
|-------------|------------|-----------------|
| S | "Industry Background" | "Digital penetration surpasses 60%, industry enters deep waters" |
| C | "Challenges Faced" | "Yet three structural contradictions constrain scaled deployment" |
| Q | "Strategic Question" | "How to move from pilot to full deployment within 18 months?" |
| A | "Solution" | "Three-phase path: Focus, Expand, Scale" |

---

## Data Contextualization (Never Present Data in Isolation)

> **Golden Rule**: Never display a single data point in isolation. Every number needs context.

| Method | Pattern | Visual Implementation |
|--------|---------|----------------------|
| **Time comparison** | "From X to Y" | Line chart + arrow annotating magnitude of change |
| **Benchmark** | "X vs industry average Y" | Bar chart with gray dashed baseline |
| **Competitive comparison** | "Us X vs Competitor Y" | Side-by-side bar chart, highlight own data |
| **Target gap** | "Actual X / Target Y" | Progress bar + gap annotation |
| **Ranking** | "Ranked #N of M" | Horizontal bar chart + highlight marker |

**Data annotation three essentials**: Every data visualization must include (1) The value itself (large bold font) (2) Comparison reference (baseline / prior period / competitor) (3) Meaning interpretation ("So what?")

```xml
<text x="160" y="280" text-anchor="middle" font-size="42" font-weight="bold" fill="#1E293B">97.3%</text>
<text x="160" y="310" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="#64748B">Industry avg 82% | Competitor A 89%</text>
<text x="160" y="335" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" fill="#059669">Leading industry by 15.3 percentage points</text>
```

---

## Pyramid Principle (Conclusion First)

> Executives don't care about your *process* — they care about *results*.

```
         ┌─────────────────┐
         │  Core Conclusion │   ← Page title / Takeaway
         └────────┬────────┘
      ┌───────────┼───────────┐
  ┌───┴───┐  ┌───┴───┐  ┌───┴───┐
  │ Arg 1 │  │ Arg 2 │  │ Arg 3 │   ← Key supporting points
  └───────┘  └───────┘  └───────┘
```

| Level | Position | Font Size |
|-------|----------|-----------|
| Core conclusion | Takeaway Box | 16-18px bold |
| Arguments | Content area body | 14-16px |
| Supporting data | Charts / cards | 12-14px |

**Contrast**: Title "Market Research Results" (wrong) → "Metaverse needs 5-10 years to reach scale" (right); Body "We researched... and found..." (wrong) → "Three arguments: (1)... (2)... (3)..." (right)

---

## MBB-level Layout Patterns

### Content Page Standard Structure (1280x720)

```
┌──────────────────────────────────┐
│ Gradient top bar (0,0 → 1280,6)  │
├──────────────────────────────────┤
│ Assertion title (x=40, y=50, 24px)│
├──────────────────────────────────┤
│ Takeaway Box (x=40, y=75,        │  ← Dark background + white text, one-sentence conclusion
│   w=1200, h=45)                  │
├──────────────────────────────────┤
│ Content area (x=40, y=140,       │  ← Charts / data / analysis
│   w=1200, h=520)                 │
├──────────────────────────────────┤
│ Source | CONFIDENTIAL | Page #    │  ← y=700, 10px
└──────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Strategic Roadmap

Three phases laid out horizontally, `<rect rx="8">` + title + action list, `<polygon>` arrows connecting:

```
Focus Core (0-6mo)  ──>  Expand Capability (6-12mo)  ──>  Scale Up (12-18mo)
x=40,w=380              x=450,w=380                     x=860,w=380
```

### Benchmarking Matrix

Horizontal table; own row highlighted in theme color, others in gray. Leading indicators marked green, lagging marked red. Use `<circle>` or `<rect>` to build score points.

### Waterfall Chart (Change Attribution)

Start → increase/decrease factors → End. Positive factors green bars, negative factors red bars, start/end points dark bars, cumulative line as dashed connector.

---

## Strategic Use of Color

MBB-level color usage is extremely restrained — color serves information:

| Purpose | Method |
|---------|--------|
| **Focus** | Target data in theme color, everything else gray |
| **Reduce cognitive load** | Same series differentiated by opacity (`fill-opacity` 1.0/0.6/0.3) |
| **Semantics** | Green = positive, Red = negative, Gray = baseline |
| **Branding** | Gradient top bar / decorative lines in brand color |

**Commandments**: No more than 3 primary colors; accent color used at most 2-3 places globally; data series use same-hue depth variations, not different colors; background white or very light gray.

---

## Chart vs Table Selection Matrix

| Scenario | Recommended Form | Reason |
|----------|-----------------|--------|
| Comparing 2-7 categories | **Bar chart** | Visual comparison is intuitive |
| Time trends | **Line chart** | Time series clarity |
| Precise values / large rankings | **Table** | 50 data points in a bar chart would be chaotic |
| Proportional composition | **Donut chart** | More modern than pie charts |
| Two-dimensional positioning | **2x2 matrix** | Strategic quadrant analysis |
| Change attribution | **Waterfall chart** | Factor decomposition |

---

## Speaker Notes Style

### Narrative Tone

Targeting **executives / decision-makers**. Pyramid structure — every sentence carries information. Composed, authoritative, and insightful tone.

### Stage Direction Markers

| Marker | Purpose | Example |
|--------|---------|---------|
| `[Pause]` | Silence after key insight, let executives absorb | "This means we are missing a billion-dollar market. [Pause]" |
| `[Scan Room]` | Observe decision-makers' reactions, decide whether to elaborate | "[Scan Room] If there are questions, I can elaborate." |
| `[Data]` | Conversational number delivery | "[Data] 63% → nearly two-thirds" |
| `[Benchmark]` | Emphasize comparison baseline | "[Benchmark] Compared to the industry average of 12%, our 23% is nearly double" |
| `[Transition]` | Bridge from previous page, at start of each page's text | "[Transition] Building on the strategic framework, let's drill into the implementation path." |

### Notes Writing Guidelines

- **Pyramid structure**: Conclusion → Arguments → Details
- **Data contextualization**: Every number has a comparison reference
- **Executive language**: "The strategic implication is...", "The core insight is..."
- **Flex mechanism**: Annotate "content that can be skipped if time is tight" for flexible duration
- **Key points structure**: `Key points: (1) Core insight (2) Data support (3) Strategic implication`

### Notes Example

```markdown
# 03_strategic_path

[Transition] Having clarified the problem and the opportunity, now comes the most critical part — our response path.

We recommend a three-phase strategy. [Pause]

Phase one: Focus. Over the next six months, concentrate resources on conquering the Eastern China market.
[Data] Eastern China contributes nearly two-thirds of industry growth, [Benchmark] yet our penetration rate is only half of Competitor A's. [Pause]

Phase two: Expand. Use Eastern China as a template, replicate to Southern and Northern China.
Phase three: Scale. Leverage a digital platform for nationwide coverage.

[Scan Room] The resource allocation for phase one is in the appendix — would you like me to walk through it now?

Key points: (1) Focus-Expand-Scale three-phase approach (2) Data-backed Eastern China priority (3) 18-month full deployment
Duration: 3 minutes
Flex: [If time is tight, skip phase two and three details and go straight to financial impact]
```

---

## MBB-level Quality Checklist Supplement

### Content Level

- [ ] **SCQA complete**: Overall follows Situation-Complication-Question-Answer structure
- [ ] **Data contextualized**: Every data point has a comparison reference
- [ ] **Conclusion first**: Every page's Takeaway Box has a one-sentence conclusion
- [ ] **MECE principle**: Categorized analysis is mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive

### Visual Level

- [ ] **Color with intent**: Colors serve information delivery
- [ ] **Ample whitespace**: Not crowded; information can "breathe"
- [ ] **Visual hierarchy**: Conclusion > Arguments > Details, differentiated by font size/weight
- [ ] **Brand consistency**: Gradient top bar and footer unified throughout

### Notes Level

- [ ] **Pyramid structure**: Every page is conclusion-first
- [ ] **Stage markers complete**: [Pause] and [Scan Room] at key positions
- [ ] **Flex content annotated**: Supports flexible duration

| SCQA Element | Weak Title | MBB-level Title |
|-------------|------------|-----------------|
| S | "Industry Background" | "Digital penetration surpasses 60%, industry enters deep waters" |

| Q | "Strategic Question" | "How to move from pilot to full deployment within 18 months?" |
| A | "Solution" | "Three-phase path: Focus, Expand, Scale" |

---

## Data Contextualization (Never Present Data in Isolation)

> **Golden Rule**: Never display a single data point in isolation. Every number needs context.

| Method | Pattern | Visual Implementation |
|--------|---------|----------------------|
| **Time comparison** | "From X to Y" | Line chart + arrow annotating magnitude of change |
| **Benchmark** | "X vs industry average Y" | Bar chart with gray dashed baseline |
| **Competitive comparison** | "Us X vs Competitor Y" | Side-by-side bar chart, highlight own data |
| **Target gap** | "Actual X / Target Y" | Progress bar + gap annotation |
| **Ranking** | "Ranked #N of M" | Horizontal bar chart + highlight marker |

**Data annotation three essentials**: Every data visualization must include (1) The value itself (large bold font) (2) Comparison reference (baseline / prior period / competitor) (3) Meaning interpretation ("So what?")

```xml

<text x="160" y="310" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="#64748B">Industry avg 82% | Competitor A 89%</text>
<text x="160" y="335" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" fill="#059669">Leading industry by 15.3 percentage points</text>
```

---

## Pyramid Principle (Conclusion First)

> Executives don't care about your *process* — they care about *results*.

```
         ┌─────────────────┐
         │  Core Conclusion │   ← Page title / Takeaway
         └────────┬────────┘
      ┌───────────┼───────────┐
  ┌───┴───┐  ┌───┴───┐  ┌───┴───┐
  │ Arg 1 │  │ Arg 2 │  │ Arg 3 │   ← Key supporting points
  └───────┘  └───────┘  └───────┘
```

| Level | Position | Font Size |
|-------|----------|-----------|
| Core conclusion | Takeaway Box | 16-18px bold |

| Supporting data | Charts / cards | 12-14px |

│ Gradient top bar (0,0 → 1280,6)  │

Three phases laid out horizontally, `<rect rx="8">` + title + action list, `<polygon>` arrows connecting:

```

x=40,w=380              x=450,w=380                     x=860,w=380
```

### Waterfall Chart (Change Attribution)

Start → increase/decrease factors → End. Positive factors green bars, negative factors red bars, start/end points dark bars, cumulative line as dashed connector.

---

## Strategic Use of Color

MBB-level color usage is extremely restrained — color serves information:

| Purpose | Method |
|---------|--------|
| **Focus** | Target data in theme color, everything else gray |
| **Reduce cognitive load** | Same series differentiated by opacity (`fill-opacity` 1.0/0.6/0.3) |
| **Semantics** | Green = positive, Red = negative, Gray = baseline |
| **Branding** | Gradient top bar / decorative lines in brand color |

**Commandments**: No more than 3 primary colors; accent color used at most 2-3 places globally; data series use same-hue depth variations, not different colors; background white or very light gray.

|----------|-----------------|--------|
| Comparing 2-7 categories | **Bar chart** | Visual comparison is intuitive |
| Time trends | **Line chart** | Time series clarity |

| Proportional composition | **Donut chart** | More modern than pie charts |

Targeting **executives / decision-makers**. Pyramid structure — every sentence carries information. Composed, authoritative, and insightful tone.

### Stage Direction Markers

|--------|---------|---------|

| `[Scan Room]` | Observe decision-makers' reactions, decide whether to elaborate | "[Scan Room] If there are questions, I can elaborate." |
| `[Data]` | Conversational number delivery | "[Data] 63% → nearly two-thirds" |
| `[Benchmark]` | Emphasize comparison baseline | "[Benchmark] Compared to the industry average of 12%, our 23% is nearly double" |

- **Pyramid structure**: Conclusion → Arguments → Details
- **Data contextualization**: Every number has a comparison reference
- **Executive language**: "The strategic implication is...", "The core insight is..."

- **Key points structure**: `Key points: (1) Core insight (2) Data support (3) Strategic implication`

Phase one: Focus. Over the next six months, concentrate resources on conquering the Eastern China market.
[Data] Eastern China contributes nearly two-thirds of industry growth, [Benchmark] yet our penetration rate is only half of Competitor A's. [Pause]

Phase two: Expand. Use Eastern China as a template, replicate to Southern and Northern China.
Phase three: Scale. Leverage a digital platform for nationwide coverage.

[Scan Room] The resource allocation for phase one is in the appendix — would you like me to walk through it now?

Key points: (1) Focus-Expand-Scale three-phase approach (2) Data-backed Eastern China priority (3) 18-month full deployment
Duration: 3 minutes
Flex: [If time is tight, skip phase two and three details and go straight to financial impact]
```

1	# Shared Technical Standards
2	
3	Common technical constraints for PPT Master, eliminating cross-role file duplication.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## 1. SVG Banned Features Blacklist
8	
9	The following features are **absolutely forbidden** when generating SVGs — PPT export will break if any are used:
10	
11	| Banned Feature | Description |
12	|----------------|-------------|
13	| `clipPath` | Clipping paths |
14	| `mask` | Masks |
15	| `<style>` | Embedded stylesheets |
16	| `class` | CSS selector attributes (`id` inside `<defs>` is a legitimate reference and is NOT banned) |
17	| External CSS | External stylesheet links |
18	| `<foreignObject>` | Embedded external content |
19	| `<symbol>` + `<use>` | Symbol reference reuse |
20	| `textPath` | Text along a path |
21	| `@font-face` | Custom font declarations |
22	| `<animate*>` / `<set>` | SVG animations |
23	| `<script>` / event attributes | Scripts and interactivity |
24	| `marker` / `marker-end` | Line endpoint markers |
25	| `<iframe>` | Embedded frames |
26	
27	---
28	
29	## 2. PPT Compatibility Alternatives
30	
31	| Banned Syntax | Correct Alternative |
32	|---------------|---------------------|
33	| `fill="rgba(255,255,255,0.1)"` | `fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.1"` |
34	| `<g opacity="0.2">...</g>` | Set `fill-opacity` / `stroke-opacity` on each child element individually |
35	| `<image opacity="0.3"/>` | Overlay a `<rect fill="background-color" opacity="0.7"/>` mask layer after the image |
36	| `marker-end` arrows | Draw triangle arrows with `<polygon>` |
37	
38	**Mnemonic**: PPT does not recognize rgba, group opacity, image opacity, or markers.
39	
40	---
41	
42	## 3. Canvas Format Quick Reference
43	
44	### Presentations
45	
46	| Format | viewBox | Dimensions | Ratio |
47	|--------|---------|------------|-------|
48	| PPT 16:9 | `0 0 1280 720` | 1280x720 | 16:9 |
49	| PPT 4:3 | `0 0 1024 768` | 1024x768 | 4:3 |
50	
51	### Social Media
52	
53	| Format | viewBox | Dimensions | Ratio |
54	|--------|---------|------------|-------|
55	| Xiaohongshu (RED) | `0 0 1242 1660` | 1242x1660 | 3:4 |
56	| WeChat Moments / Instagram Post | `0 0 1080 1080` | 1080x1080 | 1:1 |
57	| Story / TikTok Vertical | `0 0 1080 1920` | 1080x1920 | 9:16 |
58	
59	### Marketing Materials
60	
61	| Format | viewBox | Dimensions | Ratio |
62	|--------|---------|------------|-------|
63	| WeChat Article Header | `0 0 900 383` | 900x383 | 2.35:1 |
64	| Landscape Banner | `0 0 1920 1080` | 1920x1080 | 16:9 |
65	| Portrait Poster | `0 0 1080 1920` | 1080x1920 | 9:16 |
66	| A4 Print (150dpi) | `0 0 1240 1754` | 1240x1754 | 1:1.414 |
67	
68	---
69	
70	## 4. Basic SVG Rules
71	
72	- **viewBox** must match the canvas dimensions (`width`/`height` must match `viewBox`)
73	- **Background**: Use `<rect>` to define the page background color
74	- **Line breaks**: Use `<tspan>` for manual line breaks; `<foreignObject>` is FORBIDDEN
75	- **Fonts**: Use system fonts only (Microsoft YaHei, Arial, Calibri, etc.); `@font-face` is FORBIDDEN
76	- **Styles**: Use inline styles only (`fill="..."` `font-size="..."`); `<style>` / `class` are FORBIDDEN (`id` inside `<defs>` is legitimate)
77	- **Colors**: Use HEX values; for transparency use `fill-opacity` / `stroke-opacity`
78	- **Image references**: `<image href="../images/xxx.png" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>`
79	- **Icon placeholders**: `<use data-icon="icon-name" x="" y="" width="48" height="48" fill="#HEX"/>` (auto-embedded during post-processing)
80	
81	---
82	
83	## 5. Post-processing Pipeline (3 Steps)
84	
85	Must be executed in order — skipping or adding extra flags is FORBIDDEN:
86	
87	```bash
88	# 1. Split speaker notes into per-page note files
89	python3 scripts/total_md_split.py <project_path>
90	
91	# 2. SVG post-processing (icon embedding, image crop/embed, text flattening, rounded rect to path)
92	python3 scripts/finalize_svg.py <project_path>
93	
94	# 3. Export PPTX (from svg_final/, embeds speaker notes by default)
95	python3 scripts/svg_to_pptx.py <project_path> -s final
96	# Default: generates native shapes (.pptx) + SVG reference (_svg.pptx)
97	```
98	
99	**Prohibited**:
100	- NEVER use `cp` as a substitute for `finalize_svg.py`
101	- NEVER export directly from `svg_output/` — MUST export from `svg_final/` (use `-s final`)
102	- NEVER add extra flags like `--only`
103	
104	**Re-run rule**: Any modification to `svg_output/` after post-processing has completed (including page revisions, additions, or deletions) requires re-running Steps 2 and 3. Step 1 only needs re-running if `notes/total.md` was also modified.
105	
106	---
107	
108	## 6. Shadow & Overlay Techniques
109	
110	> `<mask>` elements and `<image opacity="...">` are banned. Always use stacked `<rect>` or gradient overlays instead (see §2).
111	
112	### Shadow
113	
114	#### Filter Soft Shadow — Recommended
115	
116	Best for: cards, floating panels, elevated elements. `svg_to_shapes.py` automatically converts `feGaussianBlur` + `feOffset` into native PPTX `<a:outerShdw>`.
117	
118	```xml
119	<defs>
120	  <filter id="softShadow" x="-15%" y="-15%" width="140%" height="140%">
121	    <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="8"/>
122	    <feOffset dx="0" dy="4" result="offsetBlur"/>
123	    <feFlood flood-color="#000000" flood-opacity="0.08" result="shadowColor"/>
124	    <feComposite in="shadowColor" in2="offsetBlur" operator="in" result="shadow"/>
125	    <feMerge>
126	      <feMergeNode in="shadow"/>
127	      <feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/>
128	    </feMerge>
129	  </filter>
130	</defs>
131	<rect x="60" y="60" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#FFFFFF" filter="url(#softShadow)"/>
132	```
133	
134	Recommended parameters:
135	```
136	stdDeviation:   6–10     (smaller = crisper, larger = softer)
137	flood-opacity:  0.06–0.12  (keep low for a premium feel)
138	dy:             3–6      (vertical > horizontal for natural top-light)
139	dx:             0–2
140	```
141	
142	#### Colored Shadow
143	
144	Best for: accent buttons, brand-colored cards. Use the element's own color family instead of black.
145	
146	```xml
147	<filter id="colorShadow" x="-15%" y="-15%" width="140%" height="140%">
148	  <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="10"/>
149	  <feOffset dx="0" dy="6" result="offsetBlur"/>

176	#### Linear Gradient Overlay — Most Common

179	
180	```xml
181	<image href="..." x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>
182	<defs>
183	  <linearGradient id="imgOverlay" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">
184	    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0.85"/>
185	    <stop offset="55%"  stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0.30"/>
186	    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0"/>

190	```

193	
194	Best for: cover slides and full-image pages with bottom title.

196	```xml
197	<defs>

199	    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0"/>
200	    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0.72"/>
201	  </linearGradient>
202	</defs>
203	<rect x="0" y="380" width="1280" height="340" fill="url(#bottomBar)"/>
204	```

208	Best for: full-screen atmosphere slides; draws attention to the center.

218	```

# Shared Technical Standards

Common technical constraints for PPT Master, eliminating cross-role file duplication.

---

## 1. SVG Banned Features Blacklist

The following features are **absolutely forbidden** when generating SVGs — PPT export will break if any are used:

| Banned Feature | Description |
|----------------|-------------|
| `clipPath` | Clipping paths |
| `mask` | Masks |
| `<style>` | Embedded stylesheets |
| `class` | CSS selector attributes (`id` inside `<defs>` is a legitimate reference and is NOT banned) |
| External CSS | External stylesheet links |
| `<foreignObject>` | Embedded external content |
| `<symbol>` + `<use>` | Symbol reference reuse |
| `textPath` | Text along a path |
| `@font-face` | Custom font declarations |
| `<animate*>` / `<set>` | SVG animations |
| `<script>` / event attributes | Scripts and interactivity |
| `marker` / `marker-end` | Line endpoint markers |
| `<iframe>` | Embedded frames |

---

## 2. PPT Compatibility Alternatives

| Banned Syntax | Correct Alternative |
|---------------|---------------------|
| `fill="rgba(255,255,255,0.1)"` | `fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.1"` |
| `<g opacity="0.2">...</g>` | Set `fill-opacity` / `stroke-opacity` on each child element individually |
| `<image opacity="0.3"/>` | Overlay a `<rect fill="background-color" opacity="0.7"/>` mask layer after the image |
| `marker-end` arrows | Draw triangle arrows with `<polygon>` |

**Mnemonic**: PPT does not recognize rgba, group opacity, image opacity, or markers.

---

## 3. Canvas Format Quick Reference

### Presentations

| Format | viewBox | Dimensions | Ratio |
|--------|---------|------------|-------|
| PPT 16:9 | `0 0 1280 720` | 1280x720 | 16:9 |
| PPT 4:3 | `0 0 1024 768` | 1024x768 | 4:3 |

### Social Media

| Format | viewBox | Dimensions | Ratio |
|--------|---------|------------|-------|
| Xiaohongshu (RED) | `0 0 1242 1660` | 1242x1660 | 3:4 |
| WeChat Moments / Instagram Post | `0 0 1080 1080` | 1080x1080 | 1:1 |
| Story / TikTok Vertical | `0 0 1080 1920` | 1080x1920 | 9:16 |

### Marketing Materials

| Format | viewBox | Dimensions | Ratio |
|--------|---------|------------|-------|
| WeChat Article Header | `0 0 900 383` | 900x383 | 2.35:1 |
| Landscape Banner | `0 0 1920 1080` | 1920x1080 | 16:9 |
| Portrait Poster | `0 0 1080 1920` | 1080x1920 | 9:16 |
| A4 Print (150dpi) | `0 0 1240 1754` | 1240x1754 | 1:1.414 |

---

## 4. Basic SVG Rules

- **viewBox** must match the canvas dimensions (`width`/`height` must match `viewBox`)
- **Background**: Use `<rect>` to define the page background color
- **Line breaks**: Use `<tspan>` for manual line breaks; `<foreignObject>` is FORBIDDEN
- **Fonts**: Use system fonts only (Microsoft YaHei, Arial, Calibri, etc.); `@font-face` is FORBIDDEN
- **Styles**: Use inline styles only (`fill="..."` `font-size="..."`); `<style>` / `class` are FORBIDDEN (`id` inside `<defs>` is legitimate)
- **Colors**: Use HEX values; for transparency use `fill-opacity` / `stroke-opacity`
- **Image references**: `<image href="../images/xxx.png" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>`
- **Icon placeholders**: `<use data-icon="icon-name" x="" y="" width="48" height="48" fill="#HEX"/>` (auto-embedded during post-processing)

---

## 5. Post-processing Pipeline (3 Steps)

Must be executed in order — skipping or adding extra flags is FORBIDDEN:

```bash
# 1. Split speaker notes into per-page note files
python3 scripts/total_md_split.py <project_path>

# 2. SVG post-processing (icon embedding, image crop/embed, text flattening, rounded rect to path)
python3 scripts/finalize_svg.py <project_path>

# 3. Export PPTX (from svg_final/, embeds speaker notes by default)
python3 scripts/svg_to_pptx.py <project_path> -s final
# Default: generates native shapes (.pptx) + SVG reference (_svg.pptx)
```

**Prohibited**:
- NEVER use `cp` as a substitute for `finalize_svg.py`
- NEVER export directly from `svg_output/` — MUST export from `svg_final/` (use `-s final`)
- NEVER add extra flags like `--only`

**Re-run rule**: Any modification to `svg_output/` after post-processing has completed (including page revisions, additions, or deletions) requires re-running Steps 2 and 3. Step 1 only needs re-running if `notes/total.md` was also modified.

---

## 6. Shadow & Overlay Techniques

> `<mask>` elements and `<image opacity="...">` are banned. Always use stacked `<rect>` or gradient overlays instead (see §2).

### Shadow

#### Filter Soft Shadow — Recommended

Best for: cards, floating panels, elevated elements. `svg_to_shapes.py` automatically converts `feGaussianBlur` + `feOffset` into native PPTX `<a:outerShdw>`.

```xml
<defs>
  <filter id="softShadow" x="-15%" y="-15%" width="140%" height="140%">
    <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="8"/>
    <feOffset dx="0" dy="4" result="offsetBlur"/>
    <feFlood flood-color="#000000" flood-opacity="0.08" result="shadowColor"/>
    <feComposite in="shadowColor" in2="offsetBlur" operator="in" result="shadow"/>
    <feMerge>
      <feMergeNode in="shadow"/>
      <feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/>
    </feMerge>
  </filter>
</defs>
<rect x="60" y="60" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#FFFFFF" filter="url(#softShadow)"/>
```

Recommended parameters:
```
stdDeviation:   6–10     (smaller = crisper, larger = softer)
flood-opacity:  0.06–0.12  (keep low for a premium feel)
dy:             3–6      (vertical > horizontal for natural top-light)
dx:             0–2
```

#### Colored Shadow

Best for: accent buttons, brand-colored cards. Use the element's own color family instead of black.

```xml
<filter id="colorShadow" x="-15%" y="-15%" width="140%" height="140%">
  <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="10"/>
  <feOffset dx="0" dy="6" result="offsetBlur"/>
  <feFlood flood-color="#1A73E8" flood-opacity="0.20" result="shadowColor"/>
  <feComposite in="shadowColor" in2="offsetBlur" operator="in" result="shadow"/>
  <feMerge>
    <feMergeNode in="shadow"/>
    <feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/>
  </feMerge>
</filter>
```

Replace `flood-color` with the element's brand color; keep `flood-opacity` between 0.12–0.20.

#### Layered Rect Shadow — High-Compatibility Fallback

Best for: maximum compatibility with older PowerPoint versions. Stack 2–3 semi-transparent rectangles behind the main card:

```xml
<!-- Shadow layers (back to front, largest offset first) -->
<rect x="68" y="72" width="400" height="240" rx="16" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="0.03"/>
<rect x="65" y="69" width="400" height="240" rx="14" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="0.05"/>
<rect x="62" y="66" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#1A73E8" fill-opacity="0.04"/>
<!-- Main card -->
<rect x="60" y="60" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#FFFFFF"/>
```

### Image Overlay

#### Linear Gradient Overlay — Most Common

Best for: image+text pages. Gradient direction should match text position (text on left → gradient darkens toward left).

```xml
<image href="..." x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>
<defs>
  <linearGradient id="imgOverlay" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">
    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0.85"/>
    <stop offset="55%"  stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0.30"/>
    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0"/>
  </linearGradient>
</defs>
<rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#imgOverlay)"/>
```

#### Bottom Gradient Bar

Best for: cover slides and full-image pages with bottom title.

```xml
<defs>
  <linearGradient id="bottomBar" x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2="1">
    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0"/>
    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0.72"/>
  </linearGradient>
</defs>
<rect x="0" y="380" width="1280" height="340" fill="url(#bottomBar)"/>
```

#### Radial Gradient Overlay — Vignette Effect

Best for: full-screen atmosphere slides; draws attention to the center.

```xml
<defs>
  <radialGradient id="vignette" cx="50%" cy="50%" r="70%">
    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0"/>
    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0.58"/>
  </radialGradient>
</defs>
<rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#vignette)"/>
```

#### Brand Color Overlay

Best for: slides needing strong visual brand identity.

```xml
<defs>
  <linearGradient id="brandOverlay" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">
    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#005587" stop-opacity="0.80"/>

33	| `fill="rgba(255,255,255,0.1)"` | `fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.1"` |
34	| `<g opacity="0.2">...</g>` | Set `fill-opacity` / `stroke-opacity` on each child element individually |
35	| `<image opacity="0.3"/>` | Overlay a `<rect fill="background-color" opacity="0.7"/>` mask layer after the image |
36	| `marker-end` arrows | Draw triangle arrows with `<polygon>` |
37	
38	**Mnemonic**: PPT does not recognize rgba, group opacity, image opacity, or markers.
39	
40	---
41	
42	## 3. Canvas Format Quick Reference
43	
44	### Presentations
45	
46	| Format | viewBox | Dimensions | Ratio |
47	|--------|---------|------------|-------|
48	| PPT 16:9 | `0 0 1280 720` | 1280x720 | 16:9 |
49	| PPT 4:3 | `0 0 1024 768` | 1024x768 | 4:3 |
50	
51	### Social Media
52	
53	| Format | viewBox | Dimensions | Ratio |
54	|--------|---------|------------|-------|
55	| Xiaohongshu (RED) | `0 0 1242 1660` | 1242x1660 | 3:4 |
56	| WeChat Moments / Instagram Post | `0 0 1080 1080` | 1080x1080 | 1:1 |
57	| Story / TikTok Vertical | `0 0 1080 1920` | 1080x1920 | 9:16 |
58	
59	### Marketing Materials
60	
61	| Format | viewBox | Dimensions | Ratio |
62	|--------|---------|------------|-------|
63	| WeChat Article Header | `0 0 900 383` | 900x383 | 2.35:1 |
64	| Landscape Banner | `0 0 1920 1080` | 1920x1080 | 16:9 |
65	| Portrait Poster | `0 0 1080 1920` | 1080x1920 | 9:16 |
66	| A4 Print (150dpi) | `0 0 1240 1754` | 1240x1754 | 1:1.414 |
67	
68	---
69	
70	## 4. Basic SVG Rules
71	
72	- **viewBox** must match the canvas dimensions (`width`/`height` must match `viewBox`)
73	- **Background**: Use `<rect>` to define the page background color
74	- **Line breaks**: Use `<tspan>` for manual line breaks; `<foreignObject>` is FORBIDDEN
75	- **Fonts**: Use system fonts only (Microsoft YaHei, Arial, Calibri, etc.); `@font-face` is FORBIDDEN
76	- **Styles**: Use inline styles only (`fill="..."` `font-size="..."`); `<style>` / `class` are FORBIDDEN (`id` inside `<defs>` is legitimate)
77	- **Colors**: Use HEX values; for transparency use `fill-opacity` / `stroke-opacity`
78	- **Image references**: `<image href="../images/xxx.png" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>`
79	- **Icon placeholders**: `<use data-icon="icon-name" x="" y="" width="48" height="48" fill="#HEX"/>` (auto-embedded during post-processing)
80	
81	---
82	
83	## 5. Post-processing Pipeline (3 Steps)
84	
85	Must be executed in order — skipping or adding extra flags is FORBIDDEN:
86	
87	```bash
88	# 1. Split speaker notes into per-page note files
89	python3 scripts/total_md_split.py <project_path>
90	
91	# 2. SVG post-processing (icon embedding, image crop/embed, text flattening, rounded rect to path)
92	python3 scripts/finalize_svg.py <project_path>
93	
94	# 3. Export PPTX (from svg_final/, embeds speaker notes by default)
95	python3 scripts/svg_to_pptx.py <project_path> -s final
96	# Default: generates native shapes (.pptx) + SVG reference (_svg.pptx)
97	```
98	
99	**Prohibited**:
100	- NEVER use `cp` as a substitute for `finalize_svg.py`
101	- NEVER export directly from `svg_output/` — MUST export from `svg_final/` (use `-s final`)
102	- NEVER add extra flags like `--only`
103	
104	**Re-run rule**: Any modification to `svg_output/` after post-processing has completed (including page revisions, additions, or deletions) requires re-running Steps 2 and 3. Step 1 only needs re-running if `notes/total.md` was also modified.
105	
106	---
107	
108	## 6. Shadow & Overlay Techniques
109	
110	> `<mask>` elements and `<image opacity="...">` are banned. Always use stacked `<rect>` or gradient overlays instead (see §2).
111	
112	### Shadow
113	
114	#### Filter Soft Shadow — Recommended
115	
116	Best for: cards, floating panels, elevated elements. `svg_to_shapes.py` automatically converts `feGaussianBlur` + `feOffset` into native PPTX `<a:outerShdw>`.
117	
118	```xml
119	<defs>
120	  <filter id="softShadow" x="-15%" y="-15%" width="140%" height="140%">
121	    <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="8"/>
122	    <feOffset dx="0" dy="4" result="offsetBlur"/>
123	    <feFlood flood-color="#000000" flood-opacity="0.08" result="shadowColor"/>
124	    <feComposite in="shadowColor" in2="offsetBlur" operator="in" result="shadow"/>
125	    <feMerge>
126	      <feMergeNode in="shadow"/>
127	      <feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/>
128	    </feMerge>
129	  </filter>
130	</defs>
131	<rect x="60" y="60" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#FFFFFF" filter="url(#softShadow)"/>
132	```
133	
134	Recommended parameters:
135	```
136	stdDeviation:   6–10     (smaller = crisper, larger = softer)
137	flood-opacity:  0.06–0.12  (keep low for a premium feel)
138	dy:             3–6      (vertical > horizontal for natural top-light)
139	dx:             0–2
140	```
141	
142	#### Colored Shadow
143	
144	Best for: accent buttons, brand-colored cards. Use the element's own color family instead of black.
145	
146	```xml
147	<filter id="colorShadow" x="-15%" y="-15%" width="140%" height="140%">
148	  <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="10"/>
149	  <feOffset dx="0" dy="6" result="offsetBlur"/>
150	  <feFlood flood-color="#1A73E8" flood-opacity="0.20" result="shadowColor"/>
151	  <feComposite in="shadowColor" in2="offsetBlur" operator="in" result="shadow"/>
152	  <feMerge>
153	    <feMergeNode in="shadow"/>
154	    <feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/>
155	  </feMerge>
156	</filter>
157	```
158	
159	Replace `flood-color` with the element's brand color; keep `flood-opacity` between 0.12–0.20.
160	
161	#### Layered Rect Shadow — High-Compatibility Fallback
162	
163	Best for: maximum compatibility with older PowerPoint versions. Stack 2–3 semi-transparent rectangles behind the main card:
164	
165	```xml
166	<!-- Shadow layers (back to front, largest offset first) -->
167	<rect x="68" y="72" width="400" height="240" rx="16" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="0.03"/>
168	<rect x="65" y="69" width="400" height="240" rx="14" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="0.05"/>
169	<rect x="62" y="66" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#1A73E8" fill-opacity="0.04"/>
170	<!-- Main card -->
171	<rect x="60" y="60" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#FFFFFF"/>
172	```
173	
174	### Image Overlay
175	
176	#### Linear Gradient Overlay — Most Common
177	
178	Best for: image+text pages. Gradient direction should match text position (text on left → gradient darkens toward left).
179	
180	```xml
181	<image href="..." x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>
182	<defs>
183	  <linearGradient id="imgOverlay" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">
184	    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0.85"/>
185	    <stop offset="55%"  stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0.30"/>
186	    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0"/>
187	  </linearGradient>
188	</defs>
189	<rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#imgOverlay)"/>
190	```
191	
192	#### Bottom Gradient Bar
193	
194	Best for: cover slides and full-image pages with bottom title.
195	
196	```xml
197	<defs>
198	  <linearGradient id="bottomBar" x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2="1">
199	    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0"/>
200	    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0.72"/>
201	  </linearGradient>
202	</defs>
203	<rect x="0" y="380" width="1280" height="340" fill="url(#bottomBar)"/>
204	```
205	
206	#### Radial Gradient Overlay — Vignette Effect
207	
208	Best for: full-screen atmosphere slides; draws attention to the center.
209	
210	```xml
211	<defs>
212	  <radialGradient id="vignette" cx="50%" cy="50%" r="70%">
213	    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0"/>
214	    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0.58"/>
215	  </radialGradient>
216	</defs>
217	<rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#vignette)"/>
218	```
219	
220	#### Brand Color Overlay
221	
222	Best for: slides needing strong visual brand identity.
223	
224	```xml
225	<defs>
226	  <linearGradient id="brandOverlay" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">
227	    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#005587" stop-opacity="0.80"/>
228	    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#005587" stop-opacity="0.10"/>
229	  </linearGradient>
230	</defs>
231	<rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#brandOverlay)"/>
232	```
233	
234	### Quick-Reference Table
235	
236	| Scenario | Recommended Technique | Avoid |
237	|----------|-----------------------|-------|
238	| Card / panel shadow | Filter soft shadow (`flood-opacity` ≤ 0.12) | Hard black shadow |
239	| Accent / CTA button | Colored shadow (same hue family) | Generic gray shadow |
240	| Text over image | Linear gradient overlay (direction matches text side) | Uniform flat opacity over whole image |
241	| Cover / full-image slide | Bottom gradient bar + brand color | Solid black overlay |
242	| Atmosphere / hero slide | Radial vignette | Unprocessed raw image |
243	| Max PPT compatibility needed | Layered rect shadow | Filter-based shadow |
244	
245	---
246	
247	## 7. Project Directory Structure
248	
249	```
250	project/
251	├── svg_output/    # Raw SVGs (Executor output, contains placeholders)
252	├── svg_final/     # Post-processed final SVGs (finalize_svg.py output)
253	├── images/        # Image assets (user-provided + AI-generated)
254	├── notes/         # Speaker notes (.md files matching SVG names)
255	│   └── total.md   # Complete speaker notes document (before splitting)
256	├── templates/     # Project templates (if any)
257	└── *.pptx         # Exported PPT file
258	```
259
