<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" viewBox="0 0 1280 720" width="1280" height="720">
  <!-- Background -->
  <rect width="1280" height="720" fill="#0F1724"/>

  <!-- Gold top accent bar -->
  <defs>
    <linearGradient id="goldBar" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="0%">
      <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#C8A84B"/>
      <stop offset="60%" stop-color="#E8C875"/>
      <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#C8A84B" stop-opacity="0.2"/>
    </linearGradient>
  </defs>
  <rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="5" fill="url(#goldBar)"/>

  <!-- Slide title -->
  <rect x="40" y="12" width="5" height="42" fill="#C8A84B"/>
  <text x="56" y="27" font-family="Arial Black, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#E8EDF5">WORK ENVIRONMENT</text>
  <text x="56" y="48" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#A8B8D0">In-Person Work Rises to 20% While Hybrid Holds Steady at 42%</text>

  <!-- Takeaway box -->
  <rect x="40" y="60" width="1200" height="42" rx="4" fill="#1A2640"/>
  <rect x="40" y="60" width="5" height="42" fill="#C8A84B"/>
  <text x="56" y="77" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#C8A84B">KEY INSIGHT:</text>
  <text x="163" y="77" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#E8EDF5">Third consecutive year of in-person growth (15%→16%→20%) — RTO trend is real, though hybrid (42%) still dominates</text>
  <text x="56" y="94" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#A8B8D0">Hybrid work is most common at 42% | Remote at 38% | In-person at 20% in 2024</text>

  <!-- ========== 3-Year Trend Bar Chart ========== -->
  <rect x="40" y="115" width="770" height="480" rx="6" fill="#1A2640"/>
  <text x="425" y="143" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#E8EDF5">Work Environment Trends — 2022 to 2024</text>

  <!-- Legend -->
  <rect x="160" y="158" width="14" height="14" rx="2" fill="#4A90D9"/>
  <text x="180" y="170" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#A8B8D0">Remote</text>
  <rect x="280" y="158" width="14" height="14" rx="2" fill="#C8A84B"/>
  <text x="300" y="170" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#A8B8D0">Hybrid</text>
  <rect x="400" y="158" width="14" height="14" rx="2" fill="#EF5350"/>
  <text x="420" y="170" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#A8B8D0">In-Person</text>

  <!-- Y-axis labels (0-50%) -->
  <!-- bottom=540, 0%=540, 50%=220; 1%=6.4px -->
  <text x="95" y="224" text-anchor="end" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#6A7E9A">50%</text>
  <text x="95" y="288" text-anchor="end" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#6A7E9A">40%</text>
  <text x="95" y="352" text-anchor="end" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#6A7E9A">30%</text>
  <text x="95" y="416" text-anchor="end" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#6A7E9A">20%</text>
  <text x="95" y="480" text-anchor="end" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#6A7E9A">10%</text>

  <!-- Grid lines -->
  <line x1="105" y1="220" x2="760" y2="220" stroke="#2E4060" stroke-width="0.8"/>
  <line x1="105" y1="284" x2="760" y2="284" stroke="#2E4060" stroke-width="0.8"/>
  <line x1="105" y1="348" x2="760" y2="348" stroke="#2E4060" stroke-width="0.8"/>
  <line x1="105" y1="412" x2="760" y2="412" stroke="#2E4060" stroke-width="0.8"/>
  <line x1="105" y1="476" x2="760" y2="476" stroke="#2E4060" stroke-width="0.8"/>

  <!-- X-axis -->
  <line x1="105" y1="540" x2="760" y2="540" stroke="#2E4060" stroke-width="1.5"/>

  <!-- bottom=540, scale: 1% = (540-220)/50 = 6.4px -->
  <!-- 2022 group: x=160-230; 2023 group: x=360-430; 2024 group: x=560-630 -->
  <!-- Remote values: 2022~46% (missing, use ~44%), 2023~46%, 2024 38% -->
  <!-- Hybrid: 42%, 42%, 42% -->
  <!-- In-person: 15%, 16%, 20% -->

  <!-- 2022 bars (Remote=44%, Hybrid=42%, In-person=15%) -->
  <text x="216" y="558" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#A8B8D0">2022</text>
  <!-- Remote 44%: height=44*6.4=282, top=540-282=258 -->
  <rect x="140" y="258" width="48" height="282" rx="3" fill="#4A90D9" fill-opacity="0.5"/>
  <text x="164" y="250" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#4A90D9">~44%</text>
  <!-- Hybrid 42%: height=42*6.4=269, top=540-269=271 -->
  <rect x="196" y="271" width="48" height="269" rx="3" fill="#C8A84B" fill-opacity="0.5"/>
  <text x="220" y="263" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#C8A84B">42%</text>
  <!-- In-person 15%: height=15*6.4=96, top=540-96=444 -->
  <rect x="252" y="444" width="48" height="96" rx="3" fill="#EF5350" fill-opacity="0.5"/>
  <text x="276" y="436" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#EF5350">15%</text>

  <!-- 2023 bars (Remote=46%, Hybrid=42%, In-person=16%) -->
  <text x="396" y="558" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#A8B8D0">2023</text>
  <!-- Remote 46%: height=46*6.4=294, top=540-294=246 -->
  <rect x="320" y="246" width="48" height="294" rx="3" fill="#4A90D9" fill-opacity="0.75"/>
  <text x="344" y="238" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#4A90D9">46%</text>
  <!-- Hybrid 42% -->
  <rect x="376" y="271" width="48" height="269" rx="3" fill="#C8A84B" fill-opacity="0.75"/>
  <text x="400" y="263" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#C8A84B">42%</text>
  <!-- In-person 16%: height=16*6.4=103, top=540-103=437 -->
  <rect x="432" y="437" width="48" height="103" rx="3" fill="#EF5350" fill-opacity="0.75"/>
  <text x="456" y="429" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#EF5350">16%</text>

  <!-- 2024 bars (Remote=38%, Hybrid=42%, In-person=20%) — highlighted -->
  <text x="596" y="558" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#E8EDF5">2024</text>
  <!-- Remote 38%: height=38*6.4=243, top=540-243=297 -->
  <rect x="520" y="297" width="48" height="243" rx="3" fill="#4A90D9"/>
  <text x="544" y="289" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#4A90D9">38%</text>
  <!-- Hybrid 42% -->
  <rect x="576" y="271" width="48" height="269" rx="3" fill="#C8A84B"/>
  <text x="600" y="263" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#C8A84B">42%</text>
  <!-- In-person 20%: height=20*6.4=128, top=540-128=412 — HIGHLIGHTED -->
  <rect x="632" y="412" width="48" height="128" rx="3" fill="#EF5350"/>
  <text x="656" y="404" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#EF5350">20%</text>

  <!-- Arrow trend for in-person -->
  <line x1="276" y1="490" x2="440" y2="488" stroke="#EF5350" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-dasharray="5,3"/>
  <line x1="440" y1="488" x2="656" y2="474" stroke="#EF5350" stroke-width="2"/>
  <!-- Arrow head -->
  <polygon points="656,474 648,468 648,480" fill="#EF5350"/>

  <!-- ========== Right panel: Key Takeaways ========== -->
  <rect x="830" y="115" width="410" height="480" rx="6" fill="#1A2640"/>
  <text x="1035" y="143" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#E8EDF5">2024 Snapshot</text>

  <!-- Donut-style stat display for 2024 -->
  <!-- Hybrid -->
  <rect x="850" y="162" width="370" height="72" rx="5" fill="#243352"/>
  <rect x="850" y="162" width="5" height="72" fill="#C8A84B"/>
  <text x="865" y="189" font-family="Arial Black, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="28" font-weight="bold" fill="#C8A84B">42%</text>
  <text x="865" y="210" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#A8B8D0">Hybrid — most common arrangement</text>
  <text x="1170" y="210" text-anchor="end" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#6A7E9A">stable vs. 2023</text>

  <!-- Remote -->
  <rect x="850" y="244" width="370" height="72" rx="5" fill="#1E2D45"/>
  <rect x="850" y="244" width="5" height="72" fill="#4A90D9"/>
  <text x="865" y="271" font-family="Arial Black, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="28" font-weight="bold" fill="#4A90D9">38%</text>
  <text x="865" y="292" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#A8B8D0">Remote — second most common</text>
  <text x="1170" y="292" text-anchor="end" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#EF5350">↓ from ~46%</text>

  <!-- In-Person -->
  <rect x="850" y="326" width="370" height="72" rx="5" fill="#243352"/>
  <rect x="850" y="326" width="5" height="72" fill="#EF5350"/>
  <text x="865" y="353" font-family="Arial Black, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="28" font-weight="bold" fill="#EF5350">20%</text>
  <text x="865" y="374" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#A8B8D0">In-Person — rising for 3rd year</text>
  <text x="1170" y="374" text-anchor="end" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#4CAF50">↑ +5pp since 2022</text>

  <!-- Strategic implication box -->
  <rect x="850" y="412" width="370" height="140" rx="4" fill="#0F1724"/>
  <rect x="850" y="412" width="370" height="2" fill="#C8A84B"/>
  <text x="870" y="435" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#C8A84B">What This Means for HR Leaders</text>
  <text x="870" y="458" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#E8EDF5">Hybrid remains the expectation, not the</text>
  <text x="870" y="474" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#E8EDF5">exception. RTO mandates risk talent attrition</text>
  <text x="870" y="490" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#E8EDF5">— especially for top technical talent who</text>
  <text x="870" y="506" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#E8EDF5">have leverage in the current market.</text>
  <text x="870" y="528" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#A8B8D0">Structure hybrid intentionally: define</text>
  <text x="870" y="544" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#A8B8D0">office days with purpose, not mandates.</text>

  <!-- Footer -->
  <line x1="40" y1="620" x2="1240" y2="620" stroke="#2E4060" stroke-width="1"/>
  <text x="40" y="640" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#6A7E9A">Source: Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2024 | survey.stackoverflow.co/2024/work</text>
  <text x="640" y="640" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#C8A84B" letter-spacing="1">CONFIDENTIAL</text>
  <text x="1240" y="640" text-anchor="end" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#6A7E9A">3</text>
</svg>

  <text x="76" y="438" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#E8EDF5">Full-stack $63K | Front-end $49K | Blockchain $86K</text>
  <text x="76" y="458" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#6A7E9A">Largest talent pool; significant variation within tier by specialization</text>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" viewBox="0 0 1280 720" width="1280" height="720">
  <!-- Background -->
  <rect width="1280" height="720" fill="#0F1724"/>

  <!-- Subtle background texture: right diagonal decoration -->
  <rect x="800" y="0" width="480" height="720" fill="#131F35" fill-opacity="0.5"/>
  <line x1="900" y1="100" x2="900" y2="680" stroke="#1E3460" stroke-width="0.7" stroke-opacity="0.4"/>
  <line x1="1000" y1="100" x2="1000" y2="680" stroke="#1E3460" stroke-width="0.7" stroke-opacity="0.4"/>
  <line x1="1100" y1="100" x2="1100" y2="680" stroke="#1E3460" stroke-width="0.7" stroke-opacity="0.4"/>
  <line x1="820" y1="200" x2="1260" y2="200" stroke="#1E3460" stroke-width="0.7" stroke-opacity="0.4"/>
  <line x1="820" y1="350" x2="1260" y2="350" stroke="#1E3460" stroke-width="0.7" stroke-opacity="0.4"/>
  <line x1="820" y1="500" x2="1260" y2="500" stroke="#1E3460" stroke-width="0.7" stroke-opacity="0.4"/>

  <!-- Gold top accent bar -->
  <defs>
    <linearGradient id="goldBar" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="0%">
      <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#C8A84B"/>
      <stop offset="60%" stop-color="#E8C875"/>
      <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#C8A84B" stop-opacity="0.2"/>
    </linearGradient>
  </defs>
  <rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="5" fill="url(#goldBar)"/>

  <!-- Slide title -->
  <rect x="40" y="12" width="5" height="42" fill="#C8A84B"/>
  <text x="56" y="27" font-family="Arial Black, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#E8EDF5">KEY TAKEAWAYS</text>
  <text x="56" y="48" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#A8B8D0">What These Trends Mean for Hiring & Retention</text>

  <!-- Takeaway box -->
  <rect x="40" y="60" width="1200" height="42" rx="4" fill="#1A2640"/>
  <rect x="40" y="60" width="5" height="42" fill="#C8A84B"/>
  <text x="56" y="77" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#C8A84B">BOTTOM LINE:</text>
  <text x="163" y="77" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#E8EDF5">Act on these five signals to stay ahead in developer talent acquisition and retention in 2024–2025</text>
  <text x="56" y="94" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#A8B8D0">Based on 65,437 respondents across 180+ countries | Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2024</text>

  <!-- ========== 5 Takeaway cards in 2 columns ========== -->

  <!-- Card 1: Full-time softening -->
  <rect x="40" y="115" width="590" height="118" rx="6" fill="#1A2640"/>
  <rect x="40" y="115" width="5" height="118" fill="#EF5350"/>
  <!-- Icon placeholder -->
  <use data-icon="arrow-trend-down" x="52" y="122" width="32" height="32" fill="#EF5350"/>
  <text x="96" y="137" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#EF5350">01 — Full-Time Employment Softening</text>
  <text x="56" y="158" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#E8EDF5">U.S. full-time employment fell from 69% to 64.8% in one year.</text>
  <text x="56" y="175" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#E8EDF5">Build scalable contractor pipelines alongside FTE hiring plans.</text>
  <text x="56" y="192" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#A8B8D0">Freelance/contract remained strong at 16.4% globally — talent pool is growing.</text>
  <text x="56" y="222" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#6A7E9A">→ Action: Revisit workforce mix ratios and contractor onboarding processes</text>

  <!-- Card 2: Hybrid dominance -->
  <rect x="650" y="115" width="590" height="118" rx="6" fill="#1A2640"/>
  <rect x="650" y="115" width="5" height="118" fill="#C8A84B"/>
  <use data-icon="home" x="662" y="122" width="32" height="32" fill="#C8A84B"/>
  <text x="706" y="137" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#C8A84B">02 — Hybrid Is the Expectation, Not Exception</text>
  <text x="666" y="158" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#E8EDF5">42% hybrid (stable), in-person rising to 20% (3rd consecutive year up).</text>
  <text x="666" y="175" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#E8EDF5">Blanket RTO mandates risk attrition of top technical talent.</text>
  <text x="666" y="192" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#A8B8D0">Remote dropped from ~46% to 38% — some convergence on hybrid.</text>
  <text x="666" y="222" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#6A7E9A">→ Action: Define structured hybrid — purpose-driven office days, not mandate-driven</text>

  <!-- Card 3: Premium roles -->
  <rect x="40" y="247" width="590" height="118" rx="6" fill="#1A2640"/>
  <rect x="40" y="247" width="5" height="118" fill="#4A90D9"/>
  <use data-icon="dollar" x="52" y="254" width="32" height="32" fill="#4A90D9"/>
  <text x="96" y="269" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#4A90D9">03 — DevRel and SRE Roles Command Premium Pay</text>
  <text x="56" y="290" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#E8EDF5">Sr. Executive ($127K), Dev Advocate ($124K), Manager ($116K) top the chart.</text>
  <text x="56" y="307" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#E8EDF5">SRE ($99K) and Cloud Infra ($97K) are the highest purely technical roles.</text>
  <text x="56" y="324" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#A8B8D0">All premium roles share 15+ years average experience — experience premium is steep.</text>
  <text x="56" y="354" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#6A7E9A">→ Action: Calibrate comp bands using experience milestones at 10yr and 15yr</text>

  <!-- Card 4: Language correlation -->
  <rect x="650" y="247" width="590" height="118" rx="6" fill="#1A2640"/>
  <rect x="650" y="247" width="5" height="118" fill="#E8C875"/>
  <use data-icon="chart-bar" x="662" y="254" width="32" height="32" fill="#E8C875"/>
  <text x="706" y="269" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#E8C875">04 — Language Choice Correlates with Pay</text>
  <text x="666" y="290" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#E8EDF5">Erlang/Clojure/Elixir devs earn $93K–$97K vs. $64K for JavaScript.</text>
  <text x="666" y="307" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#E8EDF5">Overall salary range dropped ~$10K year-over-year across all languages.</text>
  <text x="666" y="324" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#A8B8D0">Niche language scarcity creates pay premiums — not just experience depth.</text>
  <text x="666" y="354" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#6A7E9A">→ Action: Factor primary tech stack into offer benchmarks and bands</text>

  <!-- Card 5: Developer purchasing influence -->
  <rect x="40" y="379" width="1200" height="118" rx="6" fill="#1A2640"/>
  <rect x="40" y="379" width="5" height="118" fill="#4CAF50"/>
  <use data-icon="users" x="52" y="386" width="32" height="32" fill="#4CAF50"/>
  <text x="96" y="401" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#4CAF50">05 — Engage Developers in Vendor Decisions — They Drive the Choice</text>
  <text x="56" y="422" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#E8EDF5">62% of all respondents influence tech purchasing — not just management. Engineering managers at 87%, Product managers at 77%.</text>
  <text x="56" y="439" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#E8EDF5">60% prefer a build-and-buy approach. Top evaluation methods: free trial (75%) and asking other developers (73%).</text>
  <text x="56" y="456" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#A8B8D0">This has dual implications: HR tools must win developer buy-in, and vendor outreach must target ICs not just leadership.</text>
  <text x="56" y="484" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#6A7E9A">→ Action: Include senior ICs in tooling evaluations; prioritize free-trial-first procurement strategies</text>

  <!-- Source attribution banner -->
  <rect x="40" y="515" width="1200" height="50" rx="4" fill="#1A2640"/>
  <rect x="40" y="515" width="1200" height="2" fill="#C8A84B"/>
  <text x="640" y="537" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial Black, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#C8A84B">2024 Stack Overflow Developer Survey</text>
  <text x="640" y="555" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#A8B8D0">65,437 respondents · 180+ countries · survey.stackoverflow.co/2024/work</text>

  <!-- Footer -->
  <line x1="40" y1="590" x2="1240" y2="590" stroke="#2E4060" stroke-width="1"/>
  <text x="40" y="610" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#6A7E9A">Source: Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2024 | survey.stackoverflow.co/2024/work</text>
  <text x="640" y="610" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#C8A84B" letter-spacing="1">CONFIDENTIAL</text>
  <text x="1240" y="610" text-anchor="end" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#6A7E9A">8</text>
</svg>

arguments.content:
# 01_cover

[Transition] Welcome. Today we'll walk through what 65,000 developers across 180+ countries told us in 2024 — and what it means for how we hire and retain technical talent.

This deck draws exclusively from the 2024 Stack Overflow Developer Survey, the largest annual survey of its kind. [Pause]

The survey captures employment patterns, compensation benchmarks, and workplace preferences — exactly the data engineering managers and HR leaders need to make evidence-based decisions.

Key points: (1) Survey scale: 65,437 respondents, 180+ countries (2) Focus: workforce trends, compensation, work environment (3) Source: survey.stackoverflow.co/2024/work
Duration: 1 minute

---

# 02_employment_status

[Transition] Let's start with the employment picture — because the headline number conceals an important signal.

84% of developers are currently working in some capacity. That sounds strong. [Pause] But when we zoom into the U.S., we see full-time employment has dropped 4 percentage points year-over-year — from 69% to 64.8%. [Data] That's nearly 1 in 3 U.S. developers not in traditional full-time employment.

[Benchmark] Globally the number holds at 69%. The U.S. divergence is notable and accelerating. Freelance and contracting remain significant at 16.4% globally.

Regionally: U.K. and Ukraine lean toward contracting when not full-time; Germany and India toward student status. This suggests different pipeline challenges by geography.

Key points: (1) U.S. full-time employment at 64.8%, down 4pp from 2023 (2) Freelance/contract strong at 16.4% globally (3) Build contractor pipelines alongside FTE headcount models
Duration: 2.5 minutes
Flex: [If time is tight, skip regional breakdown and focus on the U.S. YoY decline]

---

# 03_work_environment

[Transition] Now let's look at where developers are working — because location policy directly affects your ability to attract and retain talent.

Hybrid is the dominant arrangement at 42%, and it has held remarkably stable. [Pause] But what's moving is in-person: 15% in 2022, 16% in 2023, 20% in 2024. Three consecutive years of growth.

[Benchmark] Remote has actually declined — from roughly 46% to 38% — as some developers return to office. But hybrid, not fully in-person, is where the market has settled.

[Scan Room] The strategic implication is clear: if you're contemplating a blanket RTO mandate, you are swimming against a strong current. 80% of the market is not fully in-person.

Key points: (1) Hybrid stable at 42% — the market norm (2) In-person rising to 20% — RTO trend real but gradual (3) Offer structured hybrid to stay competitive in talent acquisition
Duration: 2.5 minutes

---

# 04_salary_by_type

[Transition] Having established where developers are working, let's look at what they're earning — because compensation benchmarking is where this data pays off most directly.

The gap between the top and bottom is dramatic. [Data] Senior Executives earn $127K median; Front-end developers earn $49K. The spread is nearly $80,000.

[Benchmark] But the most actionable insight isn't the extremes — it's the technical premium. SRE and Cloud Infrastructure engineers, purely technical roles, earn $97–99K. [Pause] These are not managers. They are engineers who keep critical systems running, and the market prices that accordingly.

Note that experience is a strong predictor within roles. All roles above $100K share 15+ years average experience.

Key points: (1) Top technical roles (SRE, Cloud Infra) earn $97–99K — premium for reliability skills (2) Experience 15+ years is the threshold for six-figure compensation (3) Response rate 34.7% — calibrate confidence intervals accordingly
Duration: 2.5 minutes
Flex: [Skip blockchain and product manager rows if time is tight — focus on top 5 and bottom 2]

---

# 05_salary_vs_experience

[Transition] The bar chart showed the rankings. This scatter plot reveals the underlying structure — and it tells a compelling story about experience as the primary lever.

When you plot salary against experience, three clusters emerge. [Pause]

The upper-right cluster — Senior Executive, Dev Advocate, Manager — represents the experience premium. 15–17 years, $116–127K. These are not outliers; they are a consistent pattern. [Benchmark] Compare this to the lower-left: Student at $15K, 2 years. That's an 8x salary difference explained almost entirely by experience.

The mid-tier technical roles — SRE, Cloud Infra, Dev Experience — show that technical depth can reach $97–109K with 10–13 years, even without moving into management.

[Scan Room] For comp planning: flat bands across experience levels are the fastest path to losing senior talent.

Key points: (1) Experience is the strongest predictor of compensation (2) Premium cluster at 15+ years: $116K–$127K (3) Technical track reaches near-six-figures without management role
Duration: 2.5 minutes

---

# 06_salary_by_language

[Transition] Now let's layer in language — because your technology stack choices have a direct effect on your compensation benchmarks.

Niche functional languages command a significant premium. [Data] Erlang developers earn ~$97K median. Clojure ~$95K. Elixir ~$93K. [Benchmark] Compare that to JavaScript at $64K — a $30,000+ gap for roughly the same years of experience.

The mechanism is supply scarcity. Fewer developers know Erlang; those who do command a premium. This is not purely experience — Erlang has ~12 years average vs. JavaScript's ~10 years. The gap is $33K.

Two macro signals to note: [Data] Overall salaries dropped roughly $10K year-over-year. The market-wide range moved from $70–85K in 2023 to $60–75K in 2024. This likely reflects macroeconomic normalization after the 2021–2022 tech compensation peak.

Key points: (1) Niche functional languages earn $30K+ premium over mainstream (2) Supply scarcity, not just experience, drives language premium (3) Factor primary tech stack into comp bands explicitly
Duration: 2.5 minutes
Flex: [If time is tight, focus on Tier 1 vs. Tier 3 gap — skip Tier 2 and Tier 4 details]

---

# 07_company_size_purchasing

[Transition] Before we get to our recommendations, let's add two critical pieces of context: who these developers work for, and how much influence they have over technology decisions.

Nearly half — 47% — work for organizations with fewer than 100 employees. [Pause] This has profound implications for comp benchmarking: small org compensation data pulls the median down. If you're competing at a startup, you're competing in a different market than enterprise.

[Benchmark] On the purchasing side: 62% of all developers influence technology purchases. That's not just managers. Engineering managers have 87% influence. But even individual contributors are in the room.

[Data] The preferred buying approach: 60% prefer build-and-buy. 75% start with a free trial. 73% ask other developers. [Scan Room] The implication: developer advocacy and peer review are the primary purchase channels — not top-down vendor relationships.

Key points: (1) 47% of developers at sub-100 orgs — calibrate benchmarks to org size (2) 62% have purchasing influence — ICs matter in vendor selection (3) Free trial + peer review = primary evaluation pathway
Duration: 2.5 minutes

---

# 08_key_takeaways

[Transition] Let's close with the five actions this data points to.

Five signals, five actions. [Pause]

One: Full-time employment is softening in the U.S. Build your contractor pipeline now — don't wait for headcount freezes to expose the gap.

Two: Hybrid is durable. Structured hybrid beats mandate-driven RTO. Define purpose for office days.

Three: DevRel, SRE, and leadership roles command premium pay. Calibrate compensation bands at the 10-year and 15-year experience milestones — flat bands bleed senior talent.

Four: Language choice correlates with salary. Explicitly factor tech stack into offer benchmarks — a Clojure hire and a PHP hire in the same role are not the same market.

Five: Developers drive vendor decisions. 62% have influence. Engage ICs in your tooling evaluations — they are not passive recipients of tooling choices.

[Scan Room] I'll leave you with this: the developers who answered this survey are your candidates, your current employees, and your future hires. Their answers tell you exactly what they value. Use it.

Key points: (1) Five concrete actions — workforce mix, hybrid policy, comp bands, language-adjusted benchmarks, IC engagement in purchasing (2) All findings sourced from 65,437 respondents (3) Full survey at survey.stackoverflow.co/2024/work
Duration: 3 minutes
